title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Fellowship
level: Institutional category umbrella covering multiple clinical physician fellowship tracks; not one single specialty fellowship-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Physician/advanced learner background equivalent to completed core clinical medical training; this is educational level guidance, not admissions eligibility.
Working knowledge of obstetrics and gynecology, reproductive physiology, epidemiology, evidence appraisal and medical genetics terminology.
Learners without medical training should use the course only as general education and not to guide care.
objectives: Classify the five BIDMC offerings and map the correct official certifying bodies without collapsing distinct tracks or board examinations.
Apply source-grounded clinical reasoning to maternal-fetal consultation, fetal growth, prenatal testing and high-risk maternal disease.
Appraise gynecologic cancer evidence, inherited-risk signals, fertility-sparing questions and multidisciplinary roles.
Describe reproductive-endocrine and infertility evaluation logic and relevant combined genetics training pathways.
Reason about pelvic-floor symptoms and treatment categories while respecting credentialed supervision and procedure competence limits.
Use dated, authoritative open guidance, cases and videos lawfully; distinguish clinical education, accreditation standards and board blueprints.

units.title: Professional scope, reproductive justice and shared decision-making
objectives: Differentiate the general BIDMC fellowship-directory category from five named physician tracks and identify the combined genetics pathway.
Use consent, accessible communication, equity, and patient goals to structure a multidisciplinary discussion.
Separate education, board certification, accreditation, and independent clinical competence.
topics: Track taxonomy and board pathways
Shared decisions, reproductive autonomy, disability-inclusive care, and respectful language
Confidentiality, case/image permissions, and safe learning boundaries
boardDomains: ACGME professionalism, systems-based practice, patient-centered communication; mapping only, not an exam-weight claim
units.casePractice: Review BIDMC educational webinar on care for women with intellectual/developmental disabilities and discuss accessibility and consent; link only, do not extract images or case details.
units.assessment: One-page track-and-board map, with each specific fellowship, certifier, and eligibility caveat.

units.title: Maternal-fetal growth, placental function and fetal surveillance
objectives: Interpret gestational-age-specific fetal biometry and identify FGR per the cited SMFM definition.
Distinguish fetal size percentile from etiology and build a maternal/placental/fetal differential.
Explain how serial growth and umbilical-artery Doppler results inform risk assessment without treating a course as a clinical order set.
topics: FGR/SGA distinction and ultrasound growth references
Umbilical artery Doppler; NST/CTG; fetal growth trajectory
Placental, maternal, fetal and genetic causes
boardDomains: ACGME MFM FGR, ultrasound and fetal assessment; topic map, not official ABOG blueprint weighting
units.casePractice: Work through an SMFM case-of-the-week link; dynamic contents may require public account access. No image copying or rehosting.
units.assessment: Write a structured interpretation and an uncertainty statement for a fictional serial-growth vignette; no real case or management orders.

units.title: Maternal medical disease and hypertensive/metabolic pregnancy
objectives: Frame maternal risk, baseline disease and pregnancy-specific change in a problem representation.
Compare risk-prevention and disease-management questions in hypertensive disorders, cardiometabolic disease and diabetes.
Identify the need to check current local guideline versions before applying specific treatment recommendations.
topics: Hypertension and preeclampsia prevention/recognition
Gestational diabetes and cardiovascular risk
Preconception counselling, medication review and postpartum follow-up
boardDomains: ACGME MFM maternal medical complications, consultative management, preconception and postpartum care
units.casePractice: Use the linked BIDMC MFM webinars as source material for a fictional problem representation and differential; videos do not establish a complete protocol.
units.assessment: Annotated concept map plus short-answer differential and evidence-date check.

units.title: Prenatal diagnosis, fetal anomaly and genetics
objectives: Distinguish screening from diagnostic testing and explain uncertainty in prenatal results.
Integrate maternal-fetal medicine and medical genetics roles for structural anomalies, fetal growth concerns, and inherited risk.
State what a four-year combined BIDMC programme publicly says and which distinct certifying boards govern each pathway.
topics: Prenatal genetic screening/testing and counseling
Fetal anatomy and soft markers
CMA/genomic test indications as dated in the SMFM source; consent and result interpretation
Cell-free DNA screening updates: SMFM Consult Series #74 (2025); screening/diagnosis, optional sex chromosome screening, microdeletions and multifetal limits, with source-date audit
boardDomains: ACGME MFM prenatal diagnosis; ABMGG Clinical Genetics and Genomics topic mapping; no exam percentage assertion
units.casePractice: Choose an AIUM/SMFM public fetal ultrasound challenge; access conditions and reuse restrictions apply. Record only reasoning, not images/patient data.
units.assessment: Screening-versus-diagnostic-testing comparison and a genetics referral/counseling outline. Add a dated comparison that explicitly replaces the older cfDNA reference with SMFM Consult #74 (2025), preserving screening-versus-diagnostic distinction and patient choice.

units.title: Labor, induction, hemorrhage and obstetric emergencies
objectives: Organize an obstetric emergency into stabilization, differential, team roles and escalation.
Compare clinical questions addressed by induction and hemorrhage lectures without treating recorded talks as current protocol.
Explain how fetal status and maternal status jointly affect risk assessment.
topics: Induction of labor evidence and patient-centered context
Obstetric hemorrhage response, transfusion systems, escalation
Perinatal communication, safety checklists and debriefing
boardDomains: ACGME MFM intrapartum consultation, patient safety, interprofessional teamwork
units.casePractice: Review the BIDMC hemorrhage/induction webinar recording; any patient narrative remains within the original recording and must not be downloaded or rehosted.
units.assessment: Team-based written tabletop with actions sequenced by stabilization/communication/evidence review.

units.title: Infection, hematology, psychosocial and multispecialty pregnancy
objectives: Identify why pregnancy changes assessment of selected medical comorbidities.
Use consultation/referral reasoning for infection, anemia, thrombocytopenia, IBD, cardiac disease, mental health and environmental exposures.
Avoid converting a webinar into a patient-specific treatment recommendation.
topics: HIV and pregnancy
Anemia and thrombocytopenia
IBD, CVD, vaccination and environmental exposure
Perinatal anxiety/depression and multidisciplinary care
boardDomains: ACGME MFM high-risk antepartum and medical consultation
units.casePractice: Source comparison using one BIDMC public lecture and its current society/agency guidance.
units.assessment: Comorbidity consult matrix that distinguishes evidence gaps and date-sensitive claims.

units.title: Gynecologic cancer genetics, risk and adnexal masses
objectives: Develop a differential for an adnexal mass and explain why risk stratification is not itself a diagnosis.
Recognize inherited cancer risk as an indication for genetics expertise and family-history review.
Read a cancer evidence summary as evidence synthesis rather than a formal guideline.
topics: Hereditary ovarian cancer (BRCA and beyond)
Adnexal mass evaluation and referral
Germline/somatic testing concepts, consent and family implications
boardDomains: ACGME Gynecologic Oncology genetics, diagnostic reasoning, and multidisciplinary coordination
units.casePractice: Use NCI PDQ and BIDMC public webinar links; NCI summary images are licensed only within that summary. Do not copy them.
units.assessment: Tumor-board referral brief with differential, missing data and genetics questions.

units.title: Gynecologic malignancies: staging concepts, treatment and evidence appraisal
objectives: Compare treatment modalities and multidisciplinary inputs in gynecologic malignancy without assuming one treatment fits all.
Interpret trial headlines, disease setting and evidence limits before applying them.
Identify where current guideline/source verification is required for management decisions.
topics: Cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar and trophoblastic disease
Cancer in pregnancy
Surgery, systemic therapy, radiation and symptom/palliative support
boardDomains: ACGME Gynecologic Oncology malignancy domains; exact current ABOG content weighting not publicly extracted
units.casePractice: The BIDMC educational webinars are public expert lectures, not permission to reproduce any underlying clinical image. Pair the named topics with NCI professional summaries.
units.assessment: Evidence table with population, intervention, comparator, outcome, limitations, guideline status and date.

units.title: Fertility preservation, survivorship and inclusive gynecologic oncology
objectives: Describe the decision factors in fertility-sparing discussions and the limits of a one-case inference.
Coordinate oncology, REI, genetics, psychosocial and survivorship input.
Use accessible, patient-centered communication across disability and pregnancy contexts.
topics: Fertility-sparing care and oncofertility
Survivorship/surveillance as a separate question from active treatment
Cancer in pregnancy and gynecologic care for patients with disabilities
boardDomains: ACGME Gynecologic Oncology, survivorship, ethics, multidisciplinary practice
units.casePractice: Compare relevant publicly linked webinar(s) with NCI PDQ; no clinical image files or identifying case material may be copied.
units.assessment: Counseling-plan outline including patient priorities, referrals, timing uncertainty and source date.

units.title: Female pelvic medicine: anatomy, symptoms and diagnostic reasoning
objectives: Map pelvic-floor structures to common symptom clusters and potential multisystem overlap.
Build a differential for lower urinary tract, prolapse, bowel and pain symptoms.
Explain that procedural outcomes require supervised fellowship-based competence, not video observation.
topics: Pelvic floor anatomy and functional compartments
Urinary urgency/incontinence, incomplete emptying, fistula, pain and bowel symptoms
History, examination, urodynamics and diagnostic uncertainty
boardDomains: ACGME Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery; clinical evaluation and interpretation
units.casePractice: AUGS URPS fellow webinar series includes case-based panel discussions; links are for viewing only; specific runtime/de-identification/reuse rights not independently verified.
units.assessment: Symptom-to-differential map and a test-selection rationale with explicit uncertainty.

units.title: Pelvic-floor therapeutics, surgery, complications and shared decisions
objectives: Compare conservative, pharmacologic and procedural categories for pelvic-floor disorders at a conceptual level.
Identify the outcomes, complications, patient preferences and evidence needed before elective surgery.
Explain why demonstrations/videos cannot confer procedural proficiency or authorization.
topics: Prolapse and reconstructive surgery
Stress urinary incontinence and sling/bulking options
Mesh/graft, fistula, urinary tract injury, postoperative pain and research literacy
boardDomains: ACGME Urogynecology; procedure knowledge, patient safety, surgical decision-making and outcomes research
units.casePractice: AUGS public guidance and fellow webinar page; scholarly publisher access may vary; follow original terms and do not reproduce operative images.
units.assessment: Shared-decision memo comparing options without recommending a patient-specific procedure.

units.title: Reproductive endocrinology, infertility, ART and the combined genetics pathway
objectives: Build an infertility evaluation from history, age, reproductive goals, ovulation, uterine/tubal and partner factors.
Distinguish fertility preservation, ART, reproductive genetics and general population screening.
Summarize the BIDMC three-year REI and four-year MFM/Medical Genetics track structures without equating them to the broader board directory category.
topics: Ovulatory disorders, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, menopause and ART
Male-factor assessment and concurrent evaluation
IVF/embryology, oncofertility, reproductive ethics and access
Clinical genetics and ABMGG certification pathway
Concurrent partner evaluation and male-factor concepts; ASRM SMILES lecture dated 2021, requiring current AUA/ASRM guideline check
boardDomains: ACGME REI; ABMGG Clinical Genetics and Genomics; ABOG REI and MFM pathways; mapped topics, not exam weighting
units.casePractice: Use ASRM published fertility-evaluation guidance and the linked BIDMC webinars; practice vignettes are fictional unless explicitly identified as a source case.
units.assessment: Infertility evaluation plan, shared decision framework and combined-board pathway map.

assignment.title: Five-track synthesis portfolio
deliverables: (1) Track-and-board map: directory versus actual clinical programmes, with primary-source support.
(2) Fictional MFM consultation: FGR/fetal-genetics problem representation, evidence-date table, uncertainty and referral plan.
(3) Fictional gyn-oncology tumor-board evidence memo including hereditary risk, fertility and survivorship dimensions.
(4) Fictional FPMRS and REI pair of structured assessments, one pelvic-floor symptoms framework and one infertility evaluation plan.
(5) One-page licensing/access note for a chosen public case/video and one original 6–10-minute lesson.
assignment.scoring: 0–100 points. Suggested self-study benchmark ≥80 for revision only; not validated, official, or predictive of board performance.

components.name: Original practice questions
components.note: Formative, original educational questions; not official board questions or validated pass predictors.

components.name: Five-track synthesis portfolio
components.note: Rubric above; score is for learning, not credentialing.

components.name: Evidence/access audit
components.note: Source recency, free access, rights conditions, and distinction between evidence, institutional curriculum, ACGME standards and boards.

components.name: Oral explanation / case reasoning self-recording
components.note: Fictional cases only; no real patient data; no procedure assessment.

assessment.completionNotice: Passing a local quiz/portfolio does not establish mastery, eligibility, licensure, clinical competence, or board success.

studyHours.method: A 12-week self-study plan with approximately 5 hours per unit for readings, note-making, source checking and formative assignments. This is a workload plan, not measured time or accredited training. Observed video time is separately reported.

mapping.name: Maternal-Fetal Medicine (MFM)

coveredTopics: FGR/SGA distinction and ultrasound growth references
Umbilical artery Doppler; NST/CTG; fetal growth trajectory
Placental, maternal, fetal and genetic causes

unitMap.text: Maternal medical disease and hypertensive/metabolic pregnancy
coveredTopics: Hypertension and preeclampsia prevention/recognition
Gestational diabetes and cardiovascular risk
Preconception counselling, medication review and postpartum follow-up

unitMap.text: Prenatal diagnosis, fetal anomaly and genetics
coveredTopics: Prenatal genetic screening/testing and counseling
Fetal anatomy and soft markers
CMA/genomic test indications as dated in the SMFM source; consent and result interpretation
Cell-free DNA screening updates: SMFM Consult Series #74 (2025); screening/diagnosis, optional sex chromosome screening, microdeletions and multifetal limits, with source-date audit

coveredTopics: Induction of labor evidence and patient-centered context
Obstetric hemorrhage response, transfusion systems, escalation
Perinatal communication, safety checklists and debriefing

coveredTopics: HIV and pregnancy
Anemia and thrombocytopenia
IBD, CVD, vaccination and environmental exposure
Perinatal anxiety/depression and multidisciplinary care

coveredTopics: Hereditary ovarian cancer (BRCA and beyond)

Germline/somatic testing concepts, consent and family implications

unitMap.text: Gynecologic malignancies: staging concepts, treatment and evidence appraisal
coveredTopics: Cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar and trophoblastic disease
Cancer in pregnancy
Surgery, systemic therapy, radiation and symptom/palliative support

Stress urinary incontinence and sling/bulking options
Mesh/graft, fistula, urinary tract injury, postoperative pain and research literacy

unitMap.text: Reproductive endocrinology, infertility, ART and the combined genetics pathway
coveredTopics: Ovulatory disorders, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, menopause and ART
Male-factor assessment and concurrent evaluation
IVF/embryology, oncofertility, reproductive ethics and access
Clinical genetics and ABMGG certification pathway
Concurrent partner evaluation and male-factor concepts; ASRM SMILES lecture dated 2021, requiring current AUA/ASRM guideline check

topicGaps: Recorded-video minimum: met on the observed ledger (target 36 h; 38.005 h verified free external recording). Added hours are measured third-party media, not authored targets or rendered episodes.

REI coverage remains incomplete: only one new ASRM male-infertility guideline lecture was runtime/access verified. No complete, verified free lecture set was found for ART/IVF laboratory and embryology, ovarian reserve treatment, endometriosis, menopause, pediatric endocrinology, or the complete REI fellowship curriculum.

Combined MFM/Medical Genetics track: no additional independently duration-verified medical genetics lecture series was added. Original episode covers only an introductory subset of prenatal cfDNA screening; cytogenetic, biochemical, cancer, and broader prenatal genetics require further verified instruction.

FPMRS video hours increased substantially with 10 individually observed public AUGS full-length recordings, but they are supplemental lectures from 2020, not a complete current curriculum or supervised fellowship training. Five other unverified runtime recordings remain uncounted; an additional age-restricted AUGS video is explicitly excluded.

No exact ABOG/ABMGG board weighting is asserted. Current detailed ABOG eligibility content was not extracted; ABMGG training and eligibility remain with ABMGG. ACGME programme requirements, board certification pathways, institutional rotations and recordings remain distinct source types.
Original episode scripts are authored but unrecorded, unrendered and not duration-probed. Their planned target minutes are not verified hours. No human clinician review was performed.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardStatus: The source packet is a generic BIDMC OB/GYN fellowship-directory category. BIDMC publicly lists five clinical physician tracks: FPMRS, Gynecologic Oncology, MFM, MFM/Medical Genetics & Genomics (combined), and REI. ABOG maintains distinct subspecialty certification pathways for the relevant OB-GYN subspecialties; ABMGG describes a combined MFM/Medical Genetics route and dual-board eligibility. No separate unique “MFM-genetics” board is identified. Current page content for detailed ABOG eligibility is client-rendered; eligibility is not independently adjudicated here. The combined track’s specific ACGME ADS accreditation status/ID was not verified. No research-only or non-physician fellowship is listed in the directory.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course confers no board eligibility. ABOG and ABMGG eligibility, required prior certification, approved training, examinations, application rules, and current status are determined solely by each certifying board. Verify directly with the board and the ACGME public program finder. For the combined pathway, ABMGG states the joint-training approach but does not guarantee eligibility to an individual.

topicGaps: Recorded-video minimum: met on the observed ledger (target 36 h; 38.005 h verified free external recording). Added hours are measured third-party media, not authored targets or rendered episodes.

Combined MFM/Medical Genetics track: no additional independently duration-verified medical genetics lecture series was added. Original episode covers only an introductory subset of prenatal cfDNA screening; cytogenetic, biochemical, cancer, and broader prenatal genetics require further verified instruction.

FPMRS video hours increased substantially with 10 individually observed public AUGS full-length recordings, but they are supplemental lectures from 2020, not a complete current curriculum or supervised fellowship training. Five other unverified runtime recordings remain uncounted; an additional age-restricted AUGS video is explicitly excluded.

No exact ABOG/ABMGG board weighting is asserted. Current detailed ABOG eligibility content was not extracted; ABMGG training and eligibility remain with ABMGG. ACGME programme requirements, board certification pathways, institutional rotations and recordings remain distinct source types.
Original episode scripts are authored but unrecorded, unrendered and not duration-probed. Their planned target minutes are not verified hours. No human clinician review was performed.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A teaching vignette describes a singleton pregnancy with estimated fetal weight at the 8th percentile and abdominal circumference at the 11th percentile for gestational age. Under the cited SMFM definition, which statement is most accurate?

options.text: It meets the definition of fetal growth restriction because either EFW or AC below the 10th percentile qualifies.
It cannot be FGR unless both measures are below the 10th percentile.
It is FGR only if umbilical artery Doppler is abnormal.
It is FGR only if growth velocity falls by two quartiles.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SMFM Consult #52 defines FGR as sonographic EFW or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile for gestational age; this is a learning question, not a stand-alone diagnosis or plan.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient is found to have unexplained early-onset FGR at 29 weeks with a structural anomaly. Which counseling/testing framework matches SMFM Consult #52?

options.text: Screen only for infection; genetic testing is never relevant after 20 weeks.
Offer diagnostic testing including chromosomal microarray when FGR coexists with fetal malformation or polyhydramnios, regardless of gestational age; explain options and uncertainty.
Use cell-free DNA screening as a definitive diagnostic test.
Defer all testing until after delivery.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The cited SMFM consult recommends offering diagnostic testing, including CMA, when FGR is accompanied by fetal malformation and/or polyhydramnios, regardless of gestational age. Shared counseling is essential.

practiceQuestions.stem: A teaching scenario has FGR diagnosed without absent or reversed umbilical artery end-diastolic velocity. What Doppler follow-up interval does the SMFM Consult #52 recommend once FGR is diagnosed, as a general guideline statement?

options.text: Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks to assess deterioration.
Ductus venosus Doppler every day for all pregnancies.
No Doppler evaluation after diagnosis.
Middle cerebral artery Doppler weekly as the sole routine test.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SMFM recommends umbilical artery Doppler assessment every 1–2 weeks after diagnosis, with individualized frequency based on severity and findings. Local/current guidance and the complete clinical picture govern care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional FGR case has reversed end-diastolic velocity in the umbilical artery. Which description is consistent with SMFM Consult #52?

options.text: Outpatient follow-up without escalation is the default.
The consult recommends hospitalization, antenatal corticosteroids, heightened surveillance and consideration of delivery based on the entire clinical picture.
The finding is irrelevant if estimated weight exceeds the 3rd percentile.
It mandates cesarean delivery in every case regardless of context.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For REDV, the consult recommends hospitalization, antenatal corticosteroids and heightened CTG surveillance, with delivery considered in light of the full clinical scenario. It does not supply a context-free order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which Doppler studies does SMFM advise against using routinely for clinical management of early- or late-onset FGR?

options.text: Umbilical artery Doppler.
Ductus venosus, middle cerebral artery or uterine artery Doppler.
Serial ultrasound biometry.
Antenatal testing when clinically indicated.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SMFM recommends against routine use of ductus venosus, middle cerebral artery, or uterine artery Doppler for routine clinical management of FGR; distinguish that from umbilical artery assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 34-year-old fictional patient and partner present for infertility assessment; the partner contributes sperm. Which initial approach is aligned with ASRM’s fertility-evaluation committee opinion?

options.text: Evaluate only the patient first and defer partner assessment until testing is complete.
Begin evaluation of both partners at the same time and obtain a reproductive history and at least one semen analysis for the male partner when applicable.
Order a broad genetic panel before taking a history.
Wait 12 months even when there is a known condition that may impair fertility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRM emphasizes concurrent evaluation when a male partner contributes to pregnancy, including history and at least one semen analysis; pace should be tailored to age, history and known conditions.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 37-year-old seeks an infertility evaluation after five months, and history suggests a known condition that may impair fertility. Which principle from the ASRM 2021 committee opinion is most accurate?

options.text: A known fertility-impairing condition should not delay diagnostic evaluation; typical timing is six months for women aged 35 or older absent an exigent factor.
All evaluation must wait at least 12 months regardless of age or history.
Evaluation is indicated only after assisted reproduction has begun.
Age is irrelevant to evaluation timing.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRM states typical evaluation may start at 6 months for women aged 35 or older, and without delay when a condition known to cause infertility is present. Verify current committee guidance at time of use.

practiceQuestions.stem: BIDMC publicly describes a combined Maternal-Fetal Medicine and Medical Genetics & Genomics fellowship. Which statement correctly distinguishes its training structure from board status?

options.text: It is a four-year physician track with three MFM years and one Medical Genetics & Genomics year; ABMGG describes combined training pathways for both certifying-board routes, subject to each board’s actual eligibility rules.
It is a research-only postdoctoral job with no clinical specialty pathway.
It creates one unique “MFM-genetics” board examination that replaces both boards.
A public course itself establishes eligibility for the exams.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The BIDMC page describes a four-year combined track, and ABMGG describes combined training routes with both respective certifying boards. A public self-study course does not confer board eligibility; the boards make those decisions.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educational discussion uses the NCI PDQ ovarian-cancer professional summary to compare evidence. Which statement accurately describes the source?

options.text: It is a formal NCI treatment guideline with mandatory orders.
It is a peer-reviewed evidence summary maintained by the PDQ Editorial Board, not a formal guideline; its images have use permission only within PDQ context.
It is a substitute for specialist tumor-board review.
All figures are public domain and may be copied into new teaching slides.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI identifies the summary as a peer-reviewed, evidence-based resource that does not provide formal guidelines; permission statements limit its images to PDQ context.
practiceQuestions.domain: Gynecologic oncology: evidence appraisal and image rights

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner is asked to perform a pelvic-floor procedure after watching an online educational video. What is the defensible curricular response?

options.text: Video observation plus quiz completion proves procedural competence.
The video may support conceptual preparation, but procedural competence requires supervised training and formal credentialing beyond this independent course.
Board certification is automatically granted by the video provider.
A planned original clip may count as a procedure log.

practiceQuestions.rationale: BIDMC describes an actual clinical fellowship with supervised clinical and procedural training; an independent curriculum or video cannot confer competence, licensure, privileges or board eligibility.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine

No eligible observed-duration recordings were verified in this expansion; observed external ready hours remain zero and the full 36-hour target gap remains. There is no basis to infer 36 hours from 36 planned clips or from lists of lectures.

topicGaps: All 38 previously listed ASRM Grand Rounds remain runtime-unverified in the accessible evidence checked for this expansion; the additional Johns Hopkins recording is public but its complete player runtime is not exposed. None is counted until a complete duration and free playback are revalidated.

No eligible observed-duration recordings were verified in this expansion; observed external ready hours remain zero and the full 36-hour target gap remains. There is no basis to infer 36 hours from 36 planned clips or from lists of lectures.

Instructional coverage remains limited or missing for hands-on IVF and embryology laboratory practice, stimulation monitoring and ultrasound interpretation, supervised surgery/procedures, current detailed ABOG blueprint/candidate requirements, individualized genetics counseling, and ART law/ethics. These cannot be inferred from an educational transcript or a public lecture list.
Hopkins does not expose a block-by-block schedule on the page read; ABOG pages render key eligibility/blueprint content dynamically, so exact current requirements require direct official review.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 32-year-old with regular 28-day cycles presents after 13 months trying to conceive; partner contributes sperm. What is the best initial approach?

options.text: Evaluate both partners concurrently, including semen analysis, and assess ovulation/anatomy/patency based on history.
Order endometrial biopsy and postcoital testing first.
Test ovarian reserve as population screening and defer partner assessment.
Proceed directly to diagnostic laparoscopy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Concurrent couple evaluation, semen analysis and targeted female evaluation are recommended; routine invasive or low-yield tests are not.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient aged 37 has regular cycles and no red flags after 7 months of trying. What is the most defensible counseling?

options.text: An evaluation may be initiated at 6 months for age 35 or older.
Wait 18 months because regular cycles exclude infertility.
AMH alone diagnoses infertility.
No evaluation until age 40.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRM recommends evaluation/treatment consideration after 6 months at age 35 or older; regular cycles inform ovulation but do not exclude other factors.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about AMH/AFC is most accurate?

options.text: They estimate likely response to ovarian stimulation but are poor predictors of natural fertility.
They establish whether pregnancy is possible.
A normal value excludes tubal disease.
They should be used to screen every person not meeting infertility criteria.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Ovarian reserve testing is an adjunct in infertility evaluation and can guide treatment response, not a screening/sterility test.

practiceQuestions.stem: In initial evaluation when male partner contributes sperm, which plan best aligns with guidance?

options.text: Obtain reproductive history and one or more semen analyses; do female and male evaluations concurrently.
Order sperm DNA fragmentation in every patient before semen analysis.
Begin with antisperm antibody testing.
Defer male evaluation until multiple failed IVF cycles.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AUA/ASRM guideline calls for concurrent partner assessment and initial male reproductive history and semen analysis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A semen analysis shows multiple abnormalities. What is the best next step?

options.text: Interpret in clinical context and arrange evaluation by a male reproductive expert with directed workup.
Conclude that the man is sterile from morphology alone.
Start empiric testosterone to improve fertility.
Order testicular biopsy routinely.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Multiple abnormalities raise concern but results should guide management; specialist evaluation and directed tests are appropriate. Exogenous testosterone can suppress spermatogenesis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has high AMH and an anticipated high oocyte yield during stimulation. Which risk discussion is most appropriate?

options.text: These are OHSS risk factors; discuss protocol-specific prevention and individualized risk reduction.
OHSS risk is eliminated by low-dose hCG trigger alone.
Aspirin is the recommended primary prevention.
Volume expanders should routinely be used.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRM identifies elevated AMH, PCOS/PMOS and high oocyte yield as risk markers and recommends targeted mitigation; lower-dose hCG alone and aspirin are not recommended primary strategies.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a patient considered at risk of moderate/severe OHSS, which strategy is evidence-supported in ASRM guidance?

options.text: Consider antagonist stimulation, GnRH-agonist trigger and freeze-only strategy as clinically appropriate.
Use agonist protocol and hCG trigger in all cases.
Avoid individualized gonadotropin dosing.
Give albumin to every high responder.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guideline strategies include antagonist protocols, agonist trigger and freeze-only for appropriate high-response risk; choices remain individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinic reports a 40% live-birth percentage from ART cycles. What question is essential before comparing it with another clinic?

options.text: What denominator, age mix, cycle type and outcome definition were used?
Was every cycle a singleton transfer?
Were all cycles fresh and autologous?
Does the percentage guarantee an individual outcome?

practiceQuestions.rationale: Aggregate ART rates require denominator and population context; CDC reports distinct ART cycles/transfers/outcomes and treatment groups.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does a four-year combined REI-Medical Genetics pathway mean for the curriculum classification?

options.text: It is a separate combined training offering, not interchangeable with the standard REI fellowship.
It is a research-only, non-physician course.
It eliminates any REI board process.
It is the generic SOCREI directory category.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hopkins explicitly identifies two ACGME-approved offerings and describes combined REI/genetics training as four years; curricula and certification routes differ.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which interpretation best reflects the public Hopkins programme page?

options.text: It documents a clinical fellowship with clinical, surgical and research components, but not a publicly inspectable detailed rotation-by-rotation curriculum.
It publishes a complete fellow didactic catalogue and procedure counts.
It is a directory-only non-physician category.
Its page establishes board eligibility for any learner.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official page describes components and mission; the curriculum headings do not expose a detailed schedule. Independent study does not confer eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: An individual with infertility requests donor sperm. What principle best applies?

options.text: Tailor history, exam and labs to the intended treatment and patient goals; consider anatomy/patency evaluation by risk.
Require evaluation identical to all other patients regardless of goals.
Do not evaluate because there is no sperm-contributing partner.
Perform laparoscopy in every case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRM advises considering a targeted evaluation for people using donor sperm, tailoring assessment to treatment goals and risk.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the appropriate use of the ASRM microsurgery case-based video in this independent course?

options.text: Use as linked observational discussion; do not rehost images or treat viewing as procedural competence.
Copy the surgical video frames into course materials.
Count surgery watched as supervised case volume.
Use it as certification evidence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The recording is a case-based educational resource; reuse rights are not granted by public access and video does not substitute for supervised training.

title: Reproductive Health and Advocacy Fellowship
level: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship; one-year family-medicine reproductive-health/advocacy fellowship (CHA site listing)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Intended for postgraduate clinicians/family physicians pursuing advanced conceptual study; foundational medical education and family-medicine/primary-care reproductive-health knowledge are assumed.

For supervised clinical training only, refer to official programme eligibility and licensing requirements. The independent course has no admission or clinical prerequisites because it provides no clinical practice authority.

Use current U.S. MEC/SPR, WHO resources, Society of Family Planning guidance, FDA-approved labeling, institutional protocols and applicable local law. Clinical/legal recommendations can change; verify at point of care.
objectives: Apply noncoercive, patient-centered reproductive-health counseling principles.
Use current U.S. MEC/SPR as distinct evidence tools for contraceptive eligibility and method initiation/follow-up.
Explain, at a conceptual level, common contraceptive methods, emergency contraception and service integration.
Distinguish PUL from ectopic pregnancy and develop a source-based follow-up/safety-netting framework.
Compare early pregnancy-loss management options and communicate uncertainty and choice.
Describe current guideline sources for abortion-related care and identify local legal/protocol verification needs.
Recognize the boundaries between self-study, supervised clinical training, certification, licensure and procedural competence.
Design an ethical educational or advocacy/service-change project using public, current sources.

assignment.title: Reproductive-health service access and learner-education portfolio
deliverables: A 1,200–1,800-word educational case analysis based on a fictional scenario, including a patient-centered communication plan, guideline/source mapping, uncertainty and follow-up, and referral/safety-netting.
A one-page clinic service implementation proposal with a measurable access/continuity aim, stakeholders, barriers, resource assumptions, and an ethical data plan.
A 10-minute learner-teaching plan on a single unit objective with an inclusive facilitation strategy and source list.
A brief advocacy communication (draft resolution, testimony outline or op-ed abstract) that separates evidence from law/policy and uses no patient story without explicit informed consent.

rubric.criterion: Clinical source accuracy and date qualification
rubric.proficiency: Correctly distinguishes guideline scope, date, uncertainty, and local protocol/legal limits.
Uses noncoercive language, consent, accessibility, and structural context without stereotyping.
States what is known/unknown, plausible next steps, responsible follow-up, and escalation/referral.
Objectives, learner activity, formative assessment, and accessible sources align.
Specific measurable plan, credible stakeholders, privacy safeguards, and no unsupported claims.
Uses direct public links, source-level license checks, and no copied images or identifiable data.

assignment.passThreshold: Formative course completion target: 75/100 with revision encouraged. This threshold is not validated, not board-related and does not predict exam success.

assessment.method: Formative self-checks, 9 original educational multiple-choice questions with explanations, case reasoning, and portfolio rubric. No protected or copied board questions.
assessment.limitations: Questions are not validated, not official examination items, and do not predict passage of any board examination. No human clinical review has been performed. This independent course does not assess or certify clinical skills.

studyHours.basis: Proposed self-study plan, not measured instructional time: 12 units × approximately 10 hours each, including guideline reading, case reasoning, written assignments, and retrieval practice. It excludes external lecture hours, rotations, patient care and the 36-hour video production target. Adjust based on background and not a credential.

unitMap.text: Person-centered primary-care reproductive health, consent and scope
coveredTopics: Respectful intake; consent; confidentiality; trauma-informed communication; scope of practice; referral and safety-netting

unitMap.text: Contraceptive methods and method selection
coveredTopics: Combined hormonal methods; progestin-only methods; IUDs; implants; barrier, fertility-awareness and permanent methods; counseling

unitMap.text: Contraception initiation, continuation and emergency contraception
coveredTopics: Quick start; pregnancy certainty; backup; missed doses; bleeding; emergency contraception; method switching

unitMap.text: Pregnancy options, medication abortion and law-aware referral
coveredTopics: Options counseling; eligibility and assessment; informed consent; follow-up; telehealth; FDA REMS verification; access barriers

unitMap.text: Uterine aspiration concepts, preparation, complications and referral
coveredTopics: Aspiration overview; pain support; cervical preparation; retained tissue; hemorrhage/infection/perforation response pathways; referral

unitMap.text: Early pregnancy loss: diagnosis and management choices
coveredTopics: Ultrasound criteria; pregnancy loss; expectant, medical, aspiration options; grief support; follow-up

unitMap.text: Pregnancy of unknown location and ectopic pregnancy safety-netting
coveredTopics: Positive pregnancy test/no location; symptoms; risk assessment; transvaginal ultrasound; hCG trends; ectopic precautions; loss to follow-up

unitMap.text: Ultrasound and hCG interpretation for early pregnancy
coveredTopics: Pregnancy location/viability/dating; transabdominal/transvaginal terminology; uncertainty; structured reporting

unitMap.text: STI, vaginitis, cervical health and common primary-care reproductive issues
coveredTopics: STI prevention/testing; vaginitis differential; cervical screening; abnormal bleeding; endometrial biopsy context

unitMap.text: Infertility, menstrual/endocrine issues and reproductive life course
coveredTopics: Amenorrhea; PCOS differential; infertility evaluation; ovarian reserve limits; fertility preservation; menopause

unitMap.text: Reproductive justice, anti-racist and trauma-informed practice
coveredTopics: Reproductive justice; structural racism; intersectionality; disability/language access; trauma-informed care; confidentiality

unitMap.text: Teaching, quality improvement, advocacy and sustainable service implementation
coveredTopics: Teaching plan; objective feedback; service readiness; stakeholder map; QI measures; resolution/op-ed; mentorship; self-care

topicGaps: No recording met both required tests in this expansion: publicly observed runtime and verified freely playable unauthenticated access. All six pre-existing candidate entries therefore remain uncounted; the public ASRM archive lists individual full-length presentations but the direct YouTube player runtime/access could not be verified.

Substantive recording gaps remain in foundations; contraception/MEC-SPR; pregnancy options/abortion; aspiration concepts and complications; early pregnancy loss; PUL/ectopic; ultrasound/hCG; primary-care STI/cervical/reproductive endocrinology; justice/ethics; and teaching, quality improvement and advocacy.
The ASRM Grand Rounds archive is an optional REI supplement rather than a proxy for the RHAP fellowship curriculum. Member-only Society of Family Planning teaching clips/slides remain excluded.

Five source-grounded authored episodes are mapped to units 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7. They are scripts only—not rendered recordings, verified video hours, a complete curriculum replacement, or evidence of clinical competence.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship; one-year family-medicine reproductive-health/advocacy fellowship (CHA site listing)
boardNames: No RHAP-specific board examination or board credential identified; ABFM family-medicine certification/eligibility is an entry qualification, not an RHAP fellowship examination. The ABOG Complex Family Planning subspecialty examination applies to a separate OB-GYN subspecialty fellowship.
medical.boardStatus: The CHA/RHAP fellowship is expressly not ACGME-accredited. No separate certifying board or exam for this RHAP fellowship is identified in its official public materials. The program requires board-certified or board-eligible family physicians. This is distinct from the two-year ACGME-accredited Complex Family Planning fellowship and ABOG subspecialty exam pathway.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course confers no board eligibility, certification, licensure, accreditation, credit, credential, clinical privileges, or exam readiness. For official programme application criteria, the CHA page says board-certified/eligible family physician and a Massachusetts medical license; the RHAP programme-wide page’s current cycle specifies U.S.-trained board-certified/eligible family physicians and state licensure. The two pages differ on stated training completion date (July 31 vs July 1) and should be checked directly for the relevant cycle.

officialProgrammes.institution: Cambridge Health Alliance
officialProgrammes.name: Reproductive Health and Advocacy Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official CHA page calls this a one-year, full-time fellowship based at CHA, run with RHAP and working with Tufts-CHA Family Medicine residency faculty. Public description: 3 sessions/week at Malden Family Medicine Center, 2 dedicated reproductive-procedure sessions/week at CHA and 25 days at a high-volume abortion site; teaching, advocacy and purposeful inclusion activities. RHAP’s programme-wide page says approximately 20 days at a high-volume site, so these are recorded as source-specific public descriptions, not reconciled estimates. Rotations are institutional clinical training, not video hours; no case volume inferred.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Packet includes one exact institutional variant: Cambridge Health Alliance. Official CHA page uses “Reproductive Health & Advocacy Fellowship”; packet title is retained verbatim above. It identifies CHA as a Harvard Medical School teaching hospital and lists Tufts-CHA residency collaboration; this does not make the programme a Harvard residency or an ACGME fellowship. The RHAP sponsoring-organization page lists programme sites in Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey and New York, but site-specific programme detail requires account registration; those other sites are not added as CHA variants. The “Complex Family Planning Fellowship” is a different ACGME-accredited OB-GYN subspecialty and is not an alias or combined programme. This is a clinical physician fellowship, not a generic directory category, non-physician supplement, research-only postdoc, or combined certification programme.
sourceCaveats: CHA and RHAP publish different descriptions of high-volume abortion site duration (~25 days vs ~20 days); both are quoted with their source context and are not converted into case volume or lecture hours.
CHA official page says applicant residency completion by July 31; RHAP programme-wide page (current cycle) states by July 1, 2027; confirm date on the site-specific application page.
RHAP is explicitly non-ACGME. ACGME Complex Family Planning and ABOG subspecialty certification refer to a separate OB-GYN programme. No separate RHAP exam was found in official public materials.

No faculty didactic schedule, full institutional lecture library, learner assessment validation, exact programme case volume, or public site-specific variant details are exposed. RHAP site data requires registration; no login used.

The CDC page is current as checked but displays a federal court-order notice affecting page content; consult primary MMWR and current law/guidance at point of care. FDA page fetch failed, so no detailed current REMS assertion is made.

Vimeo pages were linked by Innovating Education but triggered an anti-bot verification page; YouTube runtime metadata could not be read without authentication. No workaround attempted. No candidate duration or free playback access could therefore be verified; all candidate items are uncounted.
External links may change, and standards/laws/board rules can change after the check date. No institutional accreditation, Harvard/Johns Hopkins programme status, or board eligibility is implied.
All original cases are explicitly fictional. No clinical images or patient records were copied. NLM Open-i items require case-by-case license, de-identification and attribution checks.
The final curriculum has NOT received human clinical review.

topicGaps: No recording met both required tests in this expansion: publicly observed runtime and verified freely playable unauthenticated access. All six pre-existing candidate entries therefore remain uncounted; the public ASRM archive lists individual full-length presentations but the direct YouTube player runtime/access could not be verified.

Substantive recording gaps remain in foundations; contraception/MEC-SPR; pregnancy options/abortion; aspiration concepts and complications; early pregnancy loss; PUL/ectopic; ultrasound/hCG; primary-care STI/cervical/reproductive endocrinology; justice/ethics; and teaching, quality improvement and advocacy.
The ASRM Grand Rounds archive is an optional REI supplement rather than a proxy for the RHAP fellowship curriculum. Member-only Society of Family Planning teaching clips/slides remain excluded.

Five source-grounded authored episodes are mapped to units 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7. They are scripts only—not rendered recordings, verified video hours, a complete curriculum replacement, or evidence of clinical competence.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: A patient has a positive pregnancy test. Transvaginal ultrasound shows neither intrauterine nor extrauterine pregnancy. Which term best describes the current finding?

options.text: Confirmed ectopic pregnancy
Pregnancy of unknown location
Confirmed early pregnancy loss
Confirmed intrauterine pregnancy

practiceQuestions.rationale: PUL is the descriptive state of a positive test with no IUP or EP visualized on transvaginal ultrasound. It is not by itself a final diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: An asymptomatic patient with undesired pregnancy and a documented PUL prefers immediate treatment. What is the best general principle in the SFP 2025 guidance?

options.text: No intrauterine sac means ectopic pregnancy; defer all care.
For low ectopic risk after clinician assessment, immediate medication or procedural management may be considered with clear timely follow-up.
A single hCG confirms location.
Follow-up is unnecessary after treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SFP supports individualized immediate care for asymptomatic low-risk patients who prefer it, with careful follow-up to confirm resolution; this is not a blanket protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: For medication management of a documented PUL, which follow-up element is specifically recommended by SFP 2025?

options.text: Baseline quantitative serum hCG at medication provision
No baseline testing or follow-up
A urine test on the same day is sufficient to establish resolution
Routine laparoscopy for all patients

practiceQuestions.rationale: SFP recommends a baseline quantitative hCG for a documented PUL treated with medication to aid diagnosis and follow-up.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner suggests applying a no-test abortion follow-up pathway unchanged to a patient with an ultrasound-documented PUL. What is the best response?

options.text: SFP recommends direct extrapolation.
SFP recommends against direct extrapolation because a documented PUL has a higher ectopic risk.
No-test pathways diagnose ectopic pregnancy.
Ultrasound makes follow-up unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The March 2025 Society of Family Planning recommendation advises against direct extrapolation of no-test protocols to documented PUL.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes U.S. MEC and U.S. SPR?

options.text: MEC addresses method eligibility by medical condition; SPR addresses starting, continuing and managing use.
MEC is an exam blueprint; SPR is a board credential.
Both are legal authorization for any clinician to prescribe.
Neither should be used in individualized counseling.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC distinguishes MEC (eligibility by condition/characteristic) from SPR (practice recommendations on initiation, follow-up and common use concerns); clinical circumstances remain important.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which counseling approach is most consistent with CDC’s 2024 MEC stated goals?

options.text: Use a noncoercive, person-centered method discussion and consider individual clinical circumstances.
Require one method for all patients.
Use race as a proxy for contraceptive eligibility.
Withhold all methods until unnecessary testing is completed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC frames the recommendations as reducing unnecessary barriers and supporting person-centered, noncoercive contraception while considering each person’s circumstances.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately distinguishes the RHAP Reproductive Health Care and Advocacy Fellowship from Complex Family Planning fellowship?

options.text: Both are the same ACGME-accredited two-year fellowship.
RHAP describes a one-year family-medicine fellowship and says it is not ACGME-accredited; CFP is a separate two-year ACGME-accredited OB-GYN subspecialty.
RHAP awards ABOG CFP certification.
Complex Family Planning is only a research category.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The sponsor explicitly says RHAP is not ACGME-accredited; SFP describes CFP as two-year ACGME-accredited OB-GYN subspecialty training. Do not conflate offerings or credentials.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about reproductive-health learning and procedural competence is correct?

options.text: A lecture or case worksheet confers competence to perform uterine aspiration.
A self-study course can build conceptual knowledge, but supervised training, credentialing and authorization are separate.
A planned video counts as a completed recording.
Board eligibility follows automatically from course completion.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course does not replace accredited/supervised training, licensing, credentialing or procedural assessment. A planned recording is not delivered video evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which use of an authentic clinical image from NLM Open-i is appropriate in a locally created teaching handout?

options.text: Copy any image from search results because Open-i is public.
Link to the source; before reuse, verify image/article de-identification and the item’s specific license and reuse conditions.
Remove the attribution and crop patient details.
Assume all images are public domain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free search/access is not reuse permission. Open-i provides search filters for license types; reuse requires checking the specific source article, license, attribution, modifications and privacy conditions.

title: Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (BIDMC institutional one-year, paid, non-ACGME clinical/research fellowship; 70% research / 30% clinical as described by the programme)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Physician-level study: prior medical education and working knowledge of dermatology, skin histology, pathology, oncology, clinical staging and evidence appraisal; an advanced learner should ideally have completed dermatology residency or equivalent preparation.
Ability to interpret published clinical evidence and communicate uncertainty. Non-physicians should use introductory resources and must not use this course for clinical decision-making.
Before beginning, read the scope and board notices: this is independent self-study, not clinical education, supervised experience, procedural training or credentialing.
objectives: Frame differential diagnoses for cutaneous melanoma, keratinocyte carcinomas, MCC, CTCL and skin metastases using site, morphology, evolution, pathology, immune status and prior cancers.
Interpret disease-specific pathology and stage/risk features without conflating melanoma, BCC/cSCC, MCC or CTCL systems.
Summarize evidence-based local, regional and systemic management concepts from current official sources, with dated caveats and multidisciplinary considerations.
Communicate an evidence-supported tumor-board question and articulate missing information, patient priorities, harms and uncertainty.
Apply image licensing and privacy principles when learning from authentic clinical resources.

units.title: Clinical scope, foundations, and diagnostic safety
objectives: Distinguish melanoma, keratinocyte cancers, Merkel cell carcinoma, cutaneous lymphoma, and cutaneous metastases by lineage and clinical context.
Build a problem representation that captures site, tempo, symptoms, immune status, prior cancers, and evolving lesions.
Select questions for history/examination and identify urgent escalation signals without claiming a diagnosis from a photograph.
topics: Program scope and taxonomy; epidemiology and UV/immune risk; total-skin examination; pigmented and nonpigmented lesion morphology; diagnostic uncertainty and biopsy threshold.
boardDomains: No separate Cutaneous Oncology board blueprint is published; domains here are curricular crosswalks, not an official blueprint.
units.casePractice: Compare linked melanoma and keratinocyte cancer clinical images; write a differential, uncertainty statement, and next diagnostic step. Do not diagnose a real person from the image.
units.assessment: Structured oral-style case: 5-point rubric (problem representation, differential, risk modifiers, tissue diagnosis/referral, uncertainty/safety); pass threshold 4/5 for formative progression.

units.title: Melanoma: dermoscopy, pathology, staging, and nodal reasoning
objectives: Interpret clinical evolution and dermoscopic asymmetry/patterns as suspicion features, not a diagnosis.
Explain why pathology reporting must include Breslow thickness and ulceration and distinguish melanoma staging from keratinocyte-cancer staging.
Use AJCC8 stage concepts and evaluate the role of SLNB in context; identify the NCI PDQ threshold for considering mapping/SLNB.
topics: ABCDE/EFG/ugly duckling; amelanotic/acral/nail melanoma; diagnostic excision; Breslow thickness, ulceration, margins; sentinel-node selection and limits; AJCC8; imaging only when risk warrants.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical, surgical and dermatopathology modules
Melanoma staging/management cognition; not MDS exam preparation.
units.casePractice: Use published DermNet images as comparison exercises; make a mock pathology synoptic checklist from a fictional lesion.
units.assessment: Short-answer staging worksheet; 8-point rubric: thickness, ulceration, margins, nodes, stage source, management question, uncertainty and referral.

units.title: Basal and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma risk/pathology
objectives: Differentiate BCC and invasive cSCC while retaining clinical-pathologic differential.
Classify cSCC risk using the selected staging/risk framework and avoid confusing BWH risk stratification with AJCC staging.
Identify when biopsy depth, differentiation, perineural invasion, size/site and immunosuppression affect escalation.
topics: BCC histologic patterns and risk; cSCC histologic grade/depth/perineural invasion; BWH and AJCC scope; NCCN-style treatment stratification; biopsy sampling limitations; actinic keratosis and in-situ lesions.
boardDomains: ABD CORE surgical dermatology; no formal specialty board blueprint.
units.casePractice: Compare DermNet cSCC case images and CDC NCI-sourced BCC image with text descriptions; link images only and use as non-diagnostic pattern recognition.
units.assessment: Risk-feature classification quiz, 10 items; explain why stage/risk systems are not interchangeable.

units.title: Surgical oncology concepts, Mohs, and reconstruction
objectives: Contrast standard excision, complete margin assessment, Mohs micrographic surgery, curettage/electrodesiccation and radiation as options with patient/tumor selection caveats.
Explain margin assessment in Mohs at conceptual level and limitations of sampled vertical sections.
Recognize that a video course cannot train procedural competence or authorize surgery/reconstruction.
topics: Appropriate referral; tissue conservation; margin control; frozen/permanent sections; defect closure options; functional/cosmetic considerations; perioperative shared decision-making; recurrence follow-up.
boardDomains: ABD MDS subspecialty study-guide topics are relevant only to eligible board-certified dermatologists with required accredited fellowship; this track is not qualifying.
units.casePractice: Draw a conceptual margin map from a fictional BCC/cSCC scenario; no surgical instructions or real patient data.
units.assessment: Compare-options memo (6-point rubric: risk/location, margin certainty, contraindications, patient values, referral, no procedural authorization).

units.title: Regional disease, staging investigations, and multidisciplinary planning
objectives: Choose a question-led workup using tumor type, stage, symptoms and risk rather than indiscriminate imaging.
Discuss SLNB as a staging procedure with disease-specific evidence/indication rather than assume a survival benefit.
Create a structured tumor-board summary including known facts, unknowns, pathology, imaging, comorbidity and patient preference.
topics: Regional nodes; melanoma SLNB and ultrasound surveillance; cSCC imaging in selected high-risk scenarios; MCC nodal staging; pathology review; tumor-board workflow.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical/surgical/dermatopathology reasoning; cross-specialty clinical synthesis.
units.casePractice: Mock tumor-board referral using fictional summary only.
units.assessment: One-page tumor-board note; 10-point rubric: case framing, missing data, staging source, team roles, options, uncertainty, patient goals, safety, evidence date, follow-up.

units.title: Localized and regional melanoma management
objectives: Outline localized melanoma decision points from pathology and stage to excision, nodal evaluation and observation.
Summarize selected adjuvant/neoadjuvant/systemic approaches in the current NCI PDQ while date-checking approvals and guideline updates.
Explain why recommendations depend on stage, mutation status, treatment history, comorbidity, and patient goals.
topics: Stage 0–III; resection margins at overview level; SLNB; adjuvant anti-PD-1/targeted therapy; neoadjuvant evidence; recurrence monitoring; trial referral.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical and surgical dermatology; general board cognitive prep only.
units.casePractice: Fictional stage-II/III case decision tree; students must cite the current NCI summary and state evidence limitations.
units.assessment: Evidence table comparing options (8-point rubric: correct stage, source date, option, evidence, toxicity, preference, trial, uncertainty).

units.title: Advanced melanoma and systemic therapy reasoning
objectives: Compare checkpoint blockade and molecularly targeted options at a class/mechanism level without offering treatment instructions.
Recognize immune-related toxicity as a multidisciplinary safety concern and identify situations requiring current specialist guidance.
Communicate uncertainty and shared decision-making for advanced/recurrent disease.
topics: Immune checkpoint biology; BRAF/MEK and mutation testing; unresectable/metastatic disease; adjuvant and neoadjuvant therapy; immunosuppression/transplant risks; toxicity monitoring; trial design.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical dermatology; cross-disciplinary oncology cognitive preparation.
units.casePractice: Construct a fictional multidisciplinary consult question for advanced disease; include goals and comorbidities, not a prescribed regimen.
units.assessment: Oral defense of a treatment-class comparison; rubric addresses evidence currency, contraindication awareness, toxicity, and referral.

units.title: Advanced BCC and cSCC
objectives: Identify transition from localized surgery to multidisciplinary management for unresectable/advanced disease.
Summarize NCI PDQ options for advanced cSCC and BCC, including systemic therapy categories, without extrapolating old references.
Account for transplant and autoimmune context when discussing immune checkpoint inhibitors.
topics: Locally advanced/metastatic BCC; hedgehog-pathway agents and other current options per updated references; cSCC excision/Mohs/radiation; PD-1 inhibitors; recurrence and surveillance; transplant risk.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical and surgical modules; MDS board content only if separately eligible.
units.casePractice: Fictional kidney-transplant recipient with high-risk cSCC: create questions for a tumor board, not a treatment plan.
units.assessment: Short written consult note; rubrics score risk framing, local/systemic options, graft-related risks, multidisciplinary referral, and date-check.

units.title: Merkel cell carcinoma and other aggressive rare skin cancers
objectives: Recognize the need for pathologic confirmation and prompt staging discussion for suspected MCC.
Explain the role of surgery, radiation, nodal evaluation and systemic immunotherapy in broad terms using NCI PDQ.
Acknowledge rarity and evidence limits; avoid equating historical options with current standard.
topics: MCC morphology and pathology; Merkel polyomavirus/UV etiologic concepts; AJCC staging; surgery/radiation; advanced disease checkpoint inhibitors; follow-up; angiosarcoma and other rare tumors as differential.
units.casePractice: Review DermNet MCC image page and build differential list; image license rules apply.
units.assessment: Two-minute case handoff with evidence/source and uncertainty; formative.

units.title: Cutaneous lymphoma and skin-involving malignancy mimics
objectives: Distinguish MF/Sézary syndrome from inflammatory dermatoses and secondary cutaneous involvement at a framework level.
Explain why clinical-pathologic correlation, repeated biopsies/blood staging, and subtype classification may be needed.
Recognize the distinct treatment pathways across indolent and aggressive cutaneous lymphomas.
topics: Mycosis fungoides; Sézary syndrome; CD30-positive lymphoproliferative disorders; primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas; systemic lymphoma metastases; biopsy/immunophenotype; TNMB concepts.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical dermatology and dermatopathology; no cutaneous lymphoma board within this programme.
units.casePractice: Use free PathPresenter public slide library (free sign-up) to study expert-annotated slides where available; no download/rehosting.
units.assessment: Differential matrix with explicit uncertainty and pathology needed; 8-point rubric.

units.title: Immunosuppression, cancer predisposition, prevention, and surveillance
objectives: Identify clinically important elevated-risk contexts including solid-organ transplant immunosuppression and selected inherited cancer syndromes.
Separate primary prevention from surveillance after prior skin cancer and use population-level evidence without unsupported routine-screening claims.
Discuss immunotherapy risks in transplant and autoimmune contexts without making absolute rules.
topics: Transplant-associated SCC/melanoma/MCC; UV exposure; familial melanoma/CDKN2A, BAP1 and other syndromes; sun protection; secondary prevention; follow-up; access and skin-of-color considerations.
boardDomains: ABD CORE medical and pediatric dermatology; cross-disciplinary risk communication.
units.casePractice: Analyze a fictional patient risk profile and make a counseling/referral checklist, not personal screening advice.
units.assessment: Counseling role-play rubric (respect, risk calibration, prevention, follow-up, avoiding false reassurance).

units.title: Clinical trials, evidence appraisal, ethics, and tumor-board communication
objectives: Interpret trial phase, population, comparator, endpoints, uncertainty, and limitations before translating findings.
Present a concise, source-cited multidisciplinary case with treatment goals and patient preferences.
Distinguish education from clinical care and identify privacy, image rights and conflicts-of-interest issues.
topics: Trial literacy; evidence hierarchy; quality-of-life endpoints; trial referral; shared decision-making; de-identification; image permissions; research publication and communication.
boardDomains: ABD CORE across medical/pediatric/surgical/dermatopathology; generic evidence-based clinical reasoning.
units.casePractice: Mock tumor-board conference with a fictional de-identified-by-design vignette, not an actual patient record.
units.assessment: Final integrative case conference: 20-point rubric (case framing 3, evidence 4, differential 2, options 3, harms/uncertainty 3, patient values 2, privacy/licensing 1, referral/safety 2).

assignment.title: Source-cited cutaneous oncology tumor-board brief
assignment.instructions: Using only a constructed fictional scenario, prepare a 1-page case brief for a selected malignancy. Include a problem representation, differential or confirmed histology, risk/stage elements known and unknown, current-source citations, at least two plausible management categories, patient priorities, team members to consult, evidence limitations and a no-image/no-PHI declaration. Do not write an individual treatment order.
assignment.deliverable: One-page case summary plus 5-minute recorded or live-style oral handoff; no patient data or clinical images may be submitted.

rubric.criterion: Options, risks, patient preference and multidisciplinary roles
Uncertainty, privacy, image rights and scope limits

assignment.passingInterpretation: Formative score of 15/20 is a course progression rule only; it predicts neither board performance nor clinical competence.

unitMap.text: Clinical scope, foundations, and diagnostic safety
coveredTopics: Program scope and taxonomy; epidemiology and UV/immune risk; total-skin examination; pigmented and nonpigmented lesion morphology; diagnostic uncertainty and biopsy threshold.

unitMap.text: Melanoma: dermoscopy, pathology, staging, and nodal reasoning
coveredTopics: ABCDE/EFG/ugly duckling; amelanotic/acral/nail melanoma; diagnostic excision; Breslow thickness, ulceration, margins; sentinel-node selection and limits; AJCC8; imaging only when risk warrants.

unitMap.text: Basal and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma risk/pathology
coveredTopics: BCC histologic patterns and risk; cSCC histologic grade/depth/perineural invasion; BWH and AJCC scope; NCCN-style treatment stratification; biopsy sampling limitations; actinic keratosis and in-situ lesions.

unitMap.text: Surgical oncology concepts, Mohs, and reconstruction
coveredTopics: Appropriate referral; tissue conservation; margin control; frozen/permanent sections; defect closure options; functional/cosmetic considerations; perioperative shared decision-making; recurrence follow-up.

unitMap.text: Regional disease, staging investigations, and multidisciplinary planning
coveredTopics: Regional nodes; melanoma SLNB and ultrasound surveillance; cSCC imaging in selected high-risk scenarios; MCC nodal staging; pathology review; tumor-board workflow.

unitMap.text: Localized and regional melanoma management
coveredTopics: Stage 0–III; resection margins at overview level; SLNB; adjuvant anti-PD-1/targeted therapy; neoadjuvant evidence; recurrence monitoring; trial referral.

unitMap.text: Advanced melanoma and systemic therapy reasoning
coveredTopics: Immune checkpoint biology; BRAF/MEK and mutation testing; unresectable/metastatic disease; adjuvant and neoadjuvant therapy; immunosuppression/transplant risks; toxicity monitoring; trial design.

unitMap.text: Advanced BCC and cSCC
coveredTopics: Locally advanced/metastatic BCC; hedgehog-pathway agents and other current options per updated references; cSCC excision/Mohs/radiation; PD-1 inhibitors; recurrence and surveillance; transplant risk.

unitMap.text: Merkel cell carcinoma and other aggressive rare skin cancers
coveredTopics: MCC morphology and pathology; Merkel polyomavirus/UV etiologic concepts; AJCC staging; surgery/radiation; advanced disease checkpoint inhibitors; follow-up; angiosarcoma and other rare tumors as differential.

unitMap.text: Cutaneous lymphoma and skin-involving malignancy mimics
coveredTopics: Mycosis fungoides; Sézary syndrome; CD30-positive lymphoproliferative disorders; primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas; systemic lymphoma metastases; biopsy/immunophenotype; TNMB concepts.

unitMap.text: Immunosuppression, cancer predisposition, prevention, and surveillance
coveredTopics: Transplant-associated SCC/melanoma/MCC; UV exposure; familial melanoma/CDKN2A, BAP1 and other syndromes; sun protection; secondary prevention; follow-up; access and skin-of-color considerations.

unitMap.text: Clinical trials, evidence appraisal, ethics, and tumor-board communication
coveredTopics: Trial literacy; evidence hierarchy; quality-of-life endpoints; trial referral; shared decision-making; de-identification; image permissions; research publication and communication.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (BIDMC institutional one-year, paid, non-ACGME clinical/research fellowship; 70% research / 30% clinical as described by the programme)
boardNames: American Board of Dermatology (ABD) primary dermatology certification (CORE/APPLIED pathway; not a Cutaneous Oncology-specific board exam)

American Board of Dermatology Micrographic Dermatologic Surgery (MDS) subspecialty certification exam (separate credential; from 2026, requires ACGME-accredited Micrographic Surgery and Dermatologic Oncology fellowship and other ABD requirements)
medical.boardStatus: No separate board examination or certification specific to “Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship” is identified. ABD separately provides a general dermatology certification pathway and an MDS subspecialty examination. ABD labels its MSDO fellowship “without certification” but describes the separate MDS subspecialty certification exam; starting with 2026 MDS exam all applicants must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship. This BIDMC Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship is explicitly non-ACGME, is not the ABD/ACGME MSDO training pathway, and cannot be assumed to establish MDS eligibility. ABD CORE exam assesses medical, pediatric, surgical and dermatopathology dermatology domains; this is the nearest general board-cognitive crosswalk, not an official blueprint for this fellowship.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: BIDMC says applicants must either have completed an ACGME internship and plan to apply to dermatology residency, OR have completed dermatology residency and be ABD board-eligible. This unusually broad published entry description is not equivalent to dermatology board eligibility for all fellows. For 2026 onward, the ABD MDS exam requires an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship and other board requirements; BIDMC describes this position as non-ACGME. No course enrollment/completion establishes eligibility for BIDMC training, an ACGME programme, ABD certification/MDS exam, state licensure or clinical practice. Confirm all eligibility questions directly with BIDMC/ABD.

officialProgrammes.institution: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC)
officialProgrammes.name: Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a one-year paid, non-ACGME fellowship, approximately 70% research/30% clinical. Clinical options include Pigmented Lesion Clinic, Cutaneous Oncology Program Clinic, Complex Medical Dermatology Clinic and weekly excision clinic for board-eligible fellows. Additional opportunities: Harvard dermatology residency didactics, weekly virtual tumor board, monthly BIDMC dermatology grand rounds and New England Dermatological Society meetings. Page states expectation of at least two abstracts and two manuscripts submitted. These public descriptions are opportunities/expectations, not a verified timetable or guaranteed case volume.
