officialProgrammes.name: Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory-listed institutional variant; a full internal rotation or lecture curriculum was not verified in the directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The assigned item is a named BIDMC institutional physician fellowship, not a mere generic directory category, combined degree, research-only postdoctoral job or non-physician supplement. It has a research-heavy component but its official page describes clinical clinics and patient-care learning. It is non-ACGME and does not equal ACGME Micrographic Surgery and Dermatologic Oncology (MSDO). The single packet variant is retained as BIDMC; no Harvard or Johns Hopkins variant is inferred. BU Skin Oncology and other programmes are not merged into this variant. The programme page lists Harvard Dermatology residency didactics as an educational opportunity, not a combined programme or Harvard degree.
sourceCaveats: BIDMC webpage is the authoritative source for its own programme description; the page does not publish a complete week-by-week curriculum, lecture archive, actual case counts, or a guaranteed rotation schedule.

The BIDMC fellowship is non-ACGME; do not equate it with the ACGME Micrographic Surgery and Dermatologic Oncology fellowship or infer ABD MDS exam eligibility. ABD says all 2026 onward MDS candidates must complete accredited MSDO fellowship and meet additional requirements.
The closest general dermatology board domains are the ABD CORE modules; they are not a cutaneous-oncology fellowship board blueprint. MDS is a separate subspecialty exam.

Only one unique video had an explicit public listing runtime surfaced (54:12). YouTube metadata extraction returned an anti-bot/sign-in wall; no cookies, login or workaround were used. Other directly linked public recordings with unknown runtimes are retained but excluded from counts.
YouTube page/transcript availability was observed but playback was not independently tested; duration for the one counted item relies on public result runtime display, not playback measurement.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has an invasive cutaneous melanoma reported at 0.8 mm Breslow thickness. Which statement best matches the NCI PDQ’s summary of nodal evaluation?

options.text: All melanomas at this thickness require completion lymph-node dissection.
Lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymph-node biopsy may be considered at a primary thickness of at least 0.8 mm, after individualized discussion.
A negative sentinel node eliminates the need for all follow-up.
A sentinel node biopsy is contraindicated for lesions under 2 mm.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI summarizes that mapping and SLNB can be considered to assess occult nodal metastasis for primary melanoma at least 0.8 mm thick. It is a staging decision, not a blanket instruction or a guarantee of outcome.

practiceQuestions.stem: A pathology report for a fictional invasive melanoma omits Breslow thickness and ulceration status. What is the best next cognitive step?

options.text: Assign stage based only on lesion diameter.
Request/confirm an adequate pathology report and correlate with the clinical record before staging.
Assume the lesion is in situ if no thickness is listed.
Order systemic therapy without further staging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are key pathologic/staging elements; no stage should be invented from absent data. Confirm pathology and use current staging resources.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a localized fictional cSCC, which risk framework statement is most accurate?

options.text: BWH and AJCC systems are interchangeable and apply identically to every anatomical site.
AAD highlights BWH for prognostication and NCCN stratification for practical management; cSCC staging systems have scope limits.
Anatomic location never affects risk.
A clinically clear margin makes pathology and risk features irrelevant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AAD guideline highlights specifically distinguish BWH prognostication from NCCN clinical-management stratification. System scope and risk features should be explicit.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional cSCC is on the temple of an immunosuppressed transplant recipient and the pathology notes perineural invasion. Which response is best for this learning exercise?

options.text: Call it low risk because it is small.
Escalate risk assessment and multidisciplinary review; determine extent and options from current guidance rather than choose a regimen from the vignette alone.
Assume nodal metastasis and begin chemotherapy.
Ignore immune status if the tumor was excised.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AAD/NCI risk descriptions include immune status and perineural invasion among factors that can change evaluation; individualized multidisciplinary planning is appropriate. The vignette lacks enough data for a treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes cSCC staging from melanoma staging?

options.text: PI-RADS is the staging system for skin cancers.
Use disease-specific systems; melanoma AJCC staging and cSCC risk/staging frameworks are not interchangeable.
BWH staging is a melanoma system.
Clinical photographs alone determine the pathologic stage.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Tumor-specific staging systems and scope matter; stage relies on appropriate clinical/pathologic data, not photos alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: An older fictional adult has a rapidly enlarging, painless red nodule on sun-exposed skin. What is the most useful educational inference?

options.text: MCC is confirmed clinically and needs no biopsy.
MCC belongs in the differential; biopsy and staging work-up are required to establish diagnosis/extent.
A rapidly growing red nodule is always pyogenic granuloma.
No referral is needed because MCC is rare.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI and DermNet sources describe MCC as potentially aggressive and emphasize pathologic confirmation/staging; clinical clues are not diagnostic.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional kidney transplant recipient with advanced cSCC is being discussed for PD-1 therapy. Which principle is safest?

options.text: Checkpoint therapy has no transplant-specific risks.
Potential antitumor benefit and risk of allograft rejection require specialist, multidisciplinary, preference-sensitive discussion; this course cannot choose therapy.
Transplant history permanently rules out every possible systemic treatment.
Reduce immunosuppression without consulting the transplant team.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ describes PD-1 inhibitors among systemic options for advanced cSCC, but transplant and immune status create significant complex risks. Individual decisions need treating specialists.

practiceQuestions.stem: An AAD/ABD trainee asks if this BIDMC Cutaneous Oncology Fellowship itself makes them eligible for the ABD MDS subspecialty exam in 2026. What answer is supported?

options.text: Yes; any programme containing “cutaneous oncology” is qualifying.
No eligibility can be inferred: BIDMC labels its programme non-ACGME, while ABD says 2026 MDS exam applicants must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship and meet other board requirements.
The fellowship grants automatic ABD board certification.
There is no MDS subspecialty examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: BIDMC’s programme is non-ACGME. ABD separately offers an MDS subspecialty exam and its 2025 notice says all candidates from 2026 must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship; other requirements also apply.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which image-use plan complies with DermNet’s stated free educational licence?

options.text: Download the unwatermarked original and edit it for a paid course.
Link to the source page; if using a watermarked image educationally, retain watermark, attribute/link DermNet, use noncommercially and do not distribute derivatives.
Use any image without attribution because viewing is free.
Upload images to train a classifier.

practiceQuestions.rationale: DermNet grants free watermarked image educational use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms and explicitly requires attribution/link, noncommercial use, no derivatives, no watermark removal; it prohibits use of the free images for AI training.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the video curriculum’s relationship to formal training is correct?

options.text: Completing the online modules certifies Mohs competence.
A public lecture course replaces the ACGME clinical fellowship and supervised cases.
This independent study cannot replace accredited residency/fellowship, supervised clinical experience, licensure or board eligibility.
A passing course score guarantees board examination success.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The programme is an independent education resource. Reading/viewing and quizzes cannot establish procedural competence, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility or guaranteed exam performance.

title: Dana-Farber/Mass General Brigham Hematology/Oncology Fellowships
level: Adult clinical physician subspecialty fellowship (independent educational course; not a clinical training program)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: MD/DO-level prior medical science and completed internal medicine residency expected for the clinical fellowship context; this independent course is study material, not entry/eligibility screening.
Foundational hematology, oncology, pathology, pharmacology, epidemiology, and evidence appraisal.
This is advanced educational self-study for licensed/trainee audiences; no diagnosis, prescribing, procedures or patient-care use is authorized.
objectives: Integrate clinical history, CBC/smear, pathology and molecular tests while communicating uncertainty.
Organize common adult classical hematology and malignant hematology differentials.
Explain broad hematologic and solid-tumor oncology diagnostic, treatment, supportive care, toxicity and clinical-trial concepts.
Apply current ABIM blueprint domains and locate current authoritative evidence rather than memorize static regimen details.
Use patient-centered, ethical and safe decision frameworks, escalating emergencies to supervised teams.
Distinguish specialty board certification and eligibility from institutional programme tracks and independent education.

units.title: Clinical reasoning, evidence and safe subspecialty practice

Use evidence hierarchy and distinguish guideline recommendation from local protocol.

topics: Clinical reasoning; risk communication; evidence appraisal; disparities; goals of care; toxicity escalation.
boardDomains: ABIM medical knowledge; patient care; professionalism; systems-based practice

units.assessment: Produce a structured problem representation and 3-source evidence memo; rubric: prioritization (30%), evidence/date appraisal (30%), uncertainty (20%), communication/safety (20%).

coveredTopics: RBC/platelets/plasma; alloimmunization; transfusion reactions; therapeutic apheresis; transfusion in SCD; resource stewardship.

coveredTopics: Autologous/allogeneic HCT; CAR T and bispecifics; CRS/ICANS recognition; graft-versus-host disease; survivorship and late effects.

topicGaps: Only 2.10 of the 36 target free-recording hours are verified in the current ledger; 33.90 hours remain. The added Yale set is 2:06:08 total. Authored scripts and production targets are not ready or rendered hours.

Recorded-source coverage is concentrated in a short Yale 20 DVT lesson, five leukemia videos and one hematology-emergency video. The public Yale index does not map the leukemia parts or emergency syndromes to specific diseases; mappings are title-level and not proof of comprehensive coverage.

ABIM Hematology domains remain insufficiently taught by verified recordings: CBC/morphology and red-cell/iron disease; hemostasis and thrombosis beyond the brief DVT item; transfusion medicine; classical marrow/MPN disorders; myeloma and lymphoma; transplant/cellular therapy. Consult the January 2026 blueprint and ASH/NCI primary guidance for updates.

ABIM Medical Oncology organ-site instruction is largely absent from the added recordings. The current blueprint separately lists thoracic, breast, genitourinary, gynecologic, gastrointestinal, skin/sarcoma/unknown primary, and head/neck/thyroid/CNS disease groups, as well as palliative care and clinical-research ethics. The broad original unit headings do not amount to site-specific teaching.

UNC Lineberger lists 21 solid-tumor and 13 malignant-hematology lecture items, but the complete title/runtime/free-viewing audit remains outstanding; no durationless playlists are counted. ASH enrolled 2026 review recordings are excluded as not free.

Systemic therapy, biomarkers, toxicities, genetics, transplant/cellular therapy and guideline recommendations require dated refresh against current disease-specific guidance and FDA labeling before learner use.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Adult clinical physician subspecialty fellowship (independent educational course; not a clinical training program)
boardNames: ABIM Hematology Certification Examination
ABIM Medical Oncology Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: Two distinct ABIM subspecialty certifications and examinations exist: Hematology and Medical Oncology. There is no single ABIM “Hematology/Oncology” examination. Classical Hematology and the Hematology-Focused Fellowship Track (HFFT) are institutional/focused adult training tracks, not separate ABIM boards. The named offering is a clinical physician fellowship, not a generic directory label or research-only postdoctoral position. It includes research training after the clinical year; research years do not themselves constitute an additional specialty or board. The institution lists pediatric Hematology/Oncology separately; it is outside this adult packet and pediatric board/curriculum is distinct.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: No completion of this independent self-study course confers eligibility. ABIM certification ordinarily requires prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, requisite qualifying accredited fellowship training, documented clinical competence, unrestricted license, and passing the relevant subspecialty examination. ABIM policies and eligibility can change; candidates must confirm current rules with ABIM. Dual hematology/medical oncology certification has its own combined training and clinical-time requirements; do not infer eligibility from track names.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Packet is one adult fellowship offering. Research is an embedded training component, not independently treated as a physician board specialty. The source page also describes a separate pediatric Heme/Onc fellowship and optional Medical Educator Program for Fellows; neither is included or conflated. Public institution descriptions are not ACGME accreditation confirmation or a comprehensive posted syllabus.
sourceCaveats: Public institutional page itself lists distinct adult Hematology/Oncology and Classical Hematology tracks, and separate pediatric Hematology/Oncology programme. ASH calls its hematology-focused track HFFT. Exact current institutional slot naming/board pathway requires direct programme confirmation.
ACGME document accessed is revised for 2026 effectiveness; ABIM official policy pages reflect December 2025 policy statement on captured pages. Always verify live current versions.

ABIM initial certification blueprints exist as distinct hematology and medical oncology outlines. The linked index notes approximate content categories, but numerical domain weights were not independently extracted here; none are asserted.

Public programme rotation descriptions are not enough to claim ACGME accreditation, exact programme duration at each site, eligibility of a particular candidate, patient volume, or clinical competence.

Publicly visible videos with unverified runtime or promotional/non-instructional format count zero. No proprietary/login-only ASH video is treated as free. No audio-only podcasts count as lecture video.
All practice items are original educational content, not copied or represented as ABIM questions. Clinical management evolves; validate dates and recommendations before use.
Clinical image rights are not inferred from ability to view. No patient images, records, or case images are copied into this course.
No human clinical review has been performed.

topicGaps: Only 2.10 of the 36 target free-recording hours are verified in the current ledger; 33.90 hours remain. The added Yale set is 2:06:08 total. Authored scripts and production targets are not ready or rendered hours.

Recorded-source coverage is concentrated in a short Yale 20 DVT lesson, five leukemia videos and one hematology-emergency video. The public Yale index does not map the leukemia parts or emergency syndromes to specific diseases; mappings are title-level and not proof of comprehensive coverage.

ABIM Hematology domains remain insufficiently taught by verified recordings: CBC/morphology and red-cell/iron disease; hemostasis and thrombosis beyond the brief DVT item; transfusion medicine; classical marrow/MPN disorders; myeloma and lymphoma; transplant/cellular therapy. Consult the January 2026 blueprint and ASH/NCI primary guidance for updates.

ABIM Medical Oncology organ-site instruction is largely absent from the added recordings. The current blueprint separately lists thoracic, breast, genitourinary, gynecologic, gastrointestinal, skin/sarcoma/unknown primary, and head/neck/thyroid/CNS disease groups, as well as palliative care and clinical-research ethics. The broad original unit headings do not amount to site-specific teaching.

UNC Lineberger lists 21 solid-tumor and 13 malignant-hematology lecture items, but the complete title/runtime/free-viewing audit remains outstanding; no durationless playlists are counted. ASH enrolled 2026 review recordings are excluded as not free.

Systemic therapy, biomarkers, toxicities, genetics, transplant/cellular therapy and guideline recommendations require dated refresh against current disease-specific guidance and FDA labeling before learner use.

practiceQuestions.stem: A medically stable adult has microcytosis and low ferritin without an inflammatory context. Which interpretation is most directly supported?

options.text: Iron deficiency is supported; evaluate cause and context
Thalassemia is proven
Anemia of inflammation is proven
Myelodysplasia is proven

practiceQuestions.rationale: Low ferritin in the stated setting supports depleted iron stores but does not identify the cause; assess context and investigate appropriately.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional patient with acute unilateral leg swelling and active cancer, which statement best reflects reasoning?

options.text: Cancer alone proves DVT
Use an appropriate diagnostic pathway and consider cancer-associated thrombosis and bleeding context
Start anticoagulation without assessment
A normal platelet count excludes VTE

practiceQuestions.rationale: Malignancy raises risk but is not diagnostic. Apply current diagnostic guidance and individualized bleeding/thrombosis assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner encounters an isolated prolonged aPTT before an elective procedure. Which is the best next conceptual step?

options.text: Assume hemophilia
Interpret with bleeding/thrombosis history, medication exposure and appropriate confirmatory tests
Diagnose DIC
Ignore it if PT is normal

practiceQuestions.rationale: An isolated prolonged aPTT has multiple causes, including anticoagulant effect, factor deficiency or inhibitor; history and targeted evaluation are needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about a marrow aspirate and core biopsy is most accurate?

options.text: Each provides identical information
They can be complementary; sample quality and limitations matter
A negative aspirate rules out marrow disease
Molecular testing alone replaces morphology

practiceQuestions.rationale: Aspirate, core, morphology, flow and genetics provide complementary information; inadequate or hemodilute samples can limit interpretation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with sickle cell disease has new neurologic symptoms. What is the safest educational conclusion?

options.text: Use routine outpatient follow-up
This may be an emergency; activate immediate local emergency/specialist pathway
Assume a pain crisis only
Order no assessment because genotype is known

practiceQuestions.rationale: New neurologic symptoms can indicate time-critical complications. The course does not specify treatment; urgent local protocols and expert care are required.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes ABIM subspecialty certification in this packet?

options.text: One combined exam called Hematology-Oncology only
Hematology and Medical Oncology are distinct ABIM subspecialty certifications/exams
Course completion confers eligibility
The institutional track itself awards a board

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM lists separate Hematology and Medical Oncology certification exams and separate policies; accredited training, competence, licensure and examination apply.

practiceQuestions.stem: A candidate has completed an online self-study course and asks whether it replaces required fellowship time. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Yes, any 36 video hours replace GME
No; ABIM/ACGME requirements concern accredited supervised training and this course cannot confer board eligibility
Only for classical hematology
Only if the course has quizzes

practiceQuestions.rationale: An independent course is not accredited fellowship and cannot substitute for the prescribed training or clinical competence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the best use of an NCI PDQ health-professional summary?

options.text: Treat it as a dated evidence-oriented starting resource and verify currency with current specialty guidance
Use it as a local protocol in every patient
Assume it guarantees the best option for an individual
Treat it as board eligibility documentation

practiceQuestions.rationale: PDQs are useful public, evidence-reviewed summaries but do not replace current guidelines, labeling, multidisciplinary judgment or patient-specific care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinical trial offers an investigational treatment. Which principle is appropriate?

options.text: Participation is mandatory after referral
Explain purpose, alternatives, eligibility, risks and consent; trial participation is voluntary
Enrollment guarantees benefit
Registry status removes need for consent

practiceQuestions.rationale: Informed consent, voluntary choice, eligibility and oversight are essential; trial enrollment does not guarantee benefit.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about an open educational image found in an online image bank is safest?

options.text: Free-to-view always means permission to download and reuse
Verify item-specific provenance, de-identification, attribution and license before reuse; linking only is safest here
Remove the watermark and reuse
Patient images can be copied if names are cropped

practiceQuestions.rationale: Public view does not itself license redistribution. Respect privacy, provenance, asset terms and copyright; this curriculum does not reproduce images.

topicGaps: The 36.000-hour specialty-specific floor remains unmet: 8.915 specialty hours are verified, leaving 27.085 specialty hours. The 13.192 verifiedExternalHours total also includes 2.510 foundation hours (including the pre-existing MSU infection lecture) and 1.767 supplemental survivor/trial-literacy hours; neither category substitutes for specialty-specific didactics.

Even if every counted category were treated as video hours, 22.808 hours remain to reach 36. The stricter specialty deficit is 27.085 hours because the foundation and supplement entries are not specialty lectures.

The new public corpus improves anatomy/imaging, HPV-related oropharynx, occult-primary/nodal reasoning, thyroid and minor salivary disease, microvascular reconstruction, skull-base biology, rehabilitation, survivorship, frailty, financial toxicity and clinical-trial literacy. It does not constitute complete training or an official curriculum.

Source gaps remain in current professional radiation-planning and fractionation instruction; systemic-treatment indications/regimens and toxicity management; comprehensive site-specific pathology and image interpretation; full technical reconstructive/ablative training; rare disease coverage; and current detailed professional guideline algorithms. NCCN professional content remains copyright/license-limited and is linked, not copied.

The NCI PDQs are evidence summaries, not formal patient-specific recommendations. The AHNS curriculum is society guidance, not proof of BIDMC accreditation; the AHNS directory caveat is preserved. Publicly available lecture recordings do not reveal BIDMC proprietary didactics or provide its patient volume, rotations, case logs, or supervised clinical skills.

Age-restricted AHNS videos, inaccessible/unavailable MSU candidates, and any recording lacking independently observed duration/public access remain excluded. Public video access and observed duration can change; recheck before use.
Human clinician review was not performed. The five new authored episodes are scripted only; they are not rendered, uploaded, peer-reviewed, or counted as video hours.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

topicGaps: The 36.000-hour specialty-specific floor remains unmet: 8.915 specialty hours are verified, leaving 27.085 specialty hours. The 13.192 verifiedExternalHours total also includes 2.510 foundation hours (including the pre-existing MSU infection lecture) and 1.767 supplemental survivor/trial-literacy hours; neither category substitutes for specialty-specific didactics.

Even if every counted category were treated as video hours, 22.808 hours remain to reach 36. The stricter specialty deficit is 27.085 hours because the foundation and supplement entries are not specialty lectures.

The new public corpus improves anatomy/imaging, HPV-related oropharynx, occult-primary/nodal reasoning, thyroid and minor salivary disease, microvascular reconstruction, skull-base biology, rehabilitation, survivorship, frailty, financial toxicity and clinical-trial literacy. It does not constitute complete training or an official curriculum.

Source gaps remain in current professional radiation-planning and fractionation instruction; systemic-treatment indications/regimens and toxicity management; comprehensive site-specific pathology and image interpretation; full technical reconstructive/ablative training; rare disease coverage; and current detailed professional guideline algorithms. NCCN professional content remains copyright/license-limited and is linked, not copied.

The NCI PDQs are evidence summaries, not formal patient-specific recommendations. The AHNS curriculum is society guidance, not proof of BIDMC accreditation; the AHNS directory caveat is preserved. Publicly available lecture recordings do not reveal BIDMC proprietary didactics or provide its patient volume, rotations, case logs, or supervised clinical skills.

Age-restricted AHNS videos, inaccessible/unavailable MSU candidates, and any recording lacking independently observed duration/public access remain excluded. Public video access and observed duration can change; recheck before use.
Human clinician review was not performed. The five new authored episodes are scripted only; they are not rendered, uploaded, peer-reviewed, or counted as video hours.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: an adult has a persistent unilateral neck node; a needle sample is reported as metastatic squamous carcinoma, but office examination has not identified a primary. Which reasoning step is most defensible?

options.text: Treat the node as proof of an oropharyngeal primary
Coordinate complete mucosal evaluation, appropriate imaging and pathology review; use histology/site-specific tests to refine the differential
Start treatment based on the node alone
Assume HPV-mediated cancer without testing

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes site-appropriate examination, imaging and histologic confirmation; a nodal metastasis does not by itself establish the primary site or HPV status.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: a biopsy-proven squamous lesion lies at the base of tongue. Which site/staging distinction should the learner preserve?

options.text: Treat it as anterior oral cavity cancer because it is on the tongue
It is an oropharyngeal subsite; HPV-mediated oropharyngeal staging is distinct, while p16/HPV results must be interpreted in context
Any p16-positive tumor anywhere in the head and neck is automatically HPV-mediated oropharynx
No site distinction is used

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI defines base of tongue within the oropharynx and notes staging separates HPV-mediated oropharyngeal disease; p16 does not replace site diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: after resection of an oropharyngeal squamous cancer, the report describes a positive margin and extranodal extension. What is the best educational response?

options.text: Ignore pathology because surgery is complete
Bring the high-risk pathology to a multidisciplinary discussion of postoperative radiation and concurrent systemic-treatment evidence, individualized to the patient
Assume observation is always sufficient
Choose an adjuvant regimen without considering comorbidity or current guidelines

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ describes evidence supporting addition of concurrent chemotherapy to postoperative radiation in high-risk pathology such as positive margins or extranodal extension; the actual decision belongs to the treating multidisciplinary team.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: a small, resectable p16-positive tonsillar tumor is being discussed. Which statement best reflects the cited NCI review?

options.text: HPV positivity alone mandates treatment de-escalation
Early-stage disease is commonly managed with a single modality; surgery and radiation are options, and selection requires site, function and team-level review
All patients require the same operation
HPV status removes the need for staging

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes single-modality treatment as preferred for early-stage oropharyngeal disease and notes increasing use of transoral surgery; HPV status alone is not a universal treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: an ablative operation is being considered for a lesion that may leave a complex oral cavity defect. Which reconstruction discussion is most appropriate for an educational conference?

options.text: Choose a flap solely by the tumor label
Link oncologic margins and defect anatomy with airway, swallowing, speech, nutrition and expected function; discuss reconstructive options with the relevant team
Assume reconstruction guarantees normal function
Select a microsurgical procedure based on a video alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHNS guidance treats reconstruction as an integrated oncologic and functional problem; BIDMC describes reconstructive exposure but neither source authorizes unsupervised technique selection.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: a suspicious head-and-neck lesion is FDG-avid on imaging, but the initial tissue sample is nondiagnostic. Which inference is safest?

options.text: Imaging alone proves malignancy
The imaging and pathology are discordant; arrange clinical/pathology review and decide whether additional targeted evaluation is needed
A negative sample proves benignity in every setting
The learner can make a definitive diagnosis from the scan

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ describes imaging as part of evaluation but requires histologic confirmation; discordance requires clinical reconciliation rather than false certainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: a survivor reports persistent dysphagia and weight loss after head-and-neck cancer treatment. Which is the most complete educational framing?

options.text: Treat it only as routine surveillance
Assess for recurrence or treatment-related problems while involving appropriate swallowing, speech, nutrition and supportive-care expertise
Assume the symptom proves recurrence
Recommend an intervention without clinical assessment

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI and AHNS materials place follow-up, function, rehabilitation and multidisciplinary care within head-and-neck oncology; symptoms require clinical assessment and are not diagnostic alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: an indeterminate parotid-region mass is associated with new facial weakness. Which next reasoning step is most defensible?

options.text: Assume a benign adenoma
Treat the nerve finding as a concerning feature that warrants timely specialist assessment, appropriate imaging and tissue/pathology workup
Label it a specific histology from symptoms alone
Ignore facial function when planning care

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI site-specific summaries and multidisciplinary standards support structured evaluation; symptoms raise concern but do not establish tumor histology.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fictional case: imaging suggests a sinonasal tumor with possible skull-base extension. Which is the safest educational conclusion?

options.text: A single specialty should decide without discussion
Map anatomic extent and seek multidisciplinary planning with head-and-neck/skull-base and relevant neurosurgical/radiation/pathology expertise
The imaging finding alone gives a final histology
A surgical approach can be selected from this course

practiceQuestions.rationale: BIDMC describes sinonasal and skull-base exposure and alignment with related services; AHNS guidance expects access to interdisciplinary expertise. Definitive plans require the treating team.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes certification from the BIDMC fellowship?

options.text: ABOHNS lists a separate head-and-neck oncology subspecialty examination

ABOHNS primary certification requires Written and Oral Exams after accredited residency; its current page lists other subspecialties, while AHNS fellowship certification is a training certificate, not a board exam
The AHNS fellowship certificate replaces residency
Watching course videos confers board eligibility

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABOHNS describes the primary written and oral process and lists Complex Pediatric Otolaryngology, Neurotology and Sleep Medicine as subspecialties. AHNS ATC guidelines define a fellowship certificate; BIDMC admission language is separate from this course.

title: Hematology and Medical Oncology Fellowship Program
prerequisites: MD/DO-level internal medicine knowledge (or equivalent clinical education); intended for advanced learners and physicians, not patients.
Foundational hematology/oncology, pathology, pharmacology, statistics and evidence appraisal.
This independent course does not confer clinical access, supervised practice or institutional enrollment.
objectives: Apply structured approaches to CBC, anemia, hemolysis, coagulation and thrombosis problems.
Interpret major hematologic-neoplasm workups and explain how morphology, immunophenotype, genetics, imaging and clinical criteria combine.
Frame solid-tumor assessment around pathology, stage, biomarkers, treatment intent, evidence and patient preferences.
Recognize broad categories of hematologic and oncologic emergencies and the need for urgent in-person evaluation.
Critically appraise trial design, outcomes, uncertainty, equity and survivorship needs.
Map study content to separate ABIM hematology and medical oncology blueprints without implying exam readiness.

units.title: Hematology reasoning, CBC/smear and anemia
objectives: Build a disciplined problem representation; localize anemia using indices, reticulocytes and smear; distinguish production failure from loss/destruction; select next discriminating tests.
units.topics: CBC/differential, reticulocyte response, hemolysis panel, iron/B12/folate, hemoglobin analysis; interpret smear in context; urgent red flags.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Heme: hematopoietic system; diagnosis/testing; pathophysiology.
units.casePractice: Use ASH Image Bank images only as linked, rights-checked teaching materials. Assignment: annotate an anonymized public image with differential and next test; rubric prioritizes mechanism (40%), tests (30%), uncertainty/safety (30%).
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Hemolysis, hemoglobinopathy and marrow failure
objectives: Use clinical pattern plus labs to distinguish immune, microangiopathic, enzymatic, membrane and hemoglobin causes; identify marrow-failure emergencies.
units.topics: DAT, smear, bilirubin/LDH/haptoglobin, reticulocytes; sickle/thalassemia; aplastic anemia/PNH; transfusion and pregnancy qualifiers.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Heme: red-cell disorders; bone marrow failure.
units.casePractice: Fictional written vignette with lab table only; assessment asks mechanisms and safest confirmatory tests.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Hemostasis, platelets and thrombosis
objectives: Interpret PT/aPTT/fibrinogen/platelets; separate platelet-vessel from factor disorders; reason through VTE, HIT, DIC and thrombophilia testing.
units.topics: VWD, hemophilia, acquired inhibitors, DIC/TMA distinction, anticoagulants, cancer-associated thrombosis and bleeding.
units.casePractice: ASH Image Bank (permission varies) and fictional lab-only scenarios; no patient records. Short-answer rubric: pattern recognition, confirmatory testing, differential, safe escalation.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Plasma-cell disorders and monoclonal proteins
objectives: Interpret SPEP/UPEP/immunofixation/free-light chains with renal function and clinical context; distinguish MGUS, smoldering disease, myeloma, AL amyloid and related disorders.
units.topics: CRAB/SLiM context and diagnostic criteria, myeloma complications, paraprotein-associated renal/neuropathy differential, amyloid; avoid interpreting a single assay alone.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Heme: B-cell/plasma cell neoplasms; ABIM Oncology: hematologic neoplasms.
units.casePractice: Assignment: construct a test-ordering and interpretation tree for fictional abnormal protein results; rubric: sensitivity to context and alternative diagnoses.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Leukemias, MDS and myeloproliferative neoplasms
objectives: Organize classification by lineage, morphology, immunophenotype and genetics; triage suspected APL/leukostasis; interpret risk and treatment evidence.
units.topics: AML/ALL, MDS/MPN, CML, PV/ET/MF, CLL; cytogenetic/molecular work-up, tumor lysis, response and relapse.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Heme: neoplastic disorders; Oncology blueprint: hematologic neoplasms.
units.casePractice: Read current NCI PDQ/ASH guideline. Assessment: compare diagnostic tests and explain why urgent expert care is required.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Lymphoma, cellular therapy, transplant and transfusion
objectives: Classify lymphoma/myeloma with staging and pathology; explain transplant/cell-therapy toxicities; apply transfusion principles and reaction differentials.
units.topics: Hodgkin/NHL, CAR T, HCT, GVHD, CRS/ICANS concepts, component indications, reactions, consent/refusal.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Heme: neoplastic disorders, transfusion medicine (5%), cellular therapy (8%).
units.casePractice: Link to ASH Image Bank; authenticate image type and license; use only fictional case. Written reaction-differential assignment and source-citation rubric.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Solid-tumor diagnosis, staging and biomarker reasoning
objectives: Summarize tumor type, stage and treatment intent; select tissue, staging and predictive biomarker work-up; distinguish screening, diagnosis and surveillance.
units.topics: Breast, lung, GI, GU, gynecologic, skin, CNS/head-neck; histology, stage, molecular biomarkers; evidence strength and multidisciplinary roles.
units.casePractice: NCI PDQ adult treatment summaries (not guidelines). Case: fictional pathology report; rubric rewards staging logic and biomarker relevance.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Systemic therapy: cytotoxic, endocrine, targeted and immune
objectives: Choose a treatment framework based on disease biology, stage, intent, performance status, comorbidity, biomarkers and preferences; monitor toxicities.
units.topics: Cytotoxic principles, endocrine and targeted therapy, immunotherapy, resistance, sequencing, supportive care and safety checks.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Oncology: treatment/care decisions (60%); pathophysiology/basic science (5%).
units.casePractice: Assignment: evidence table compares options from current public PDQ/trial sources; no dosing protocol or patient-specific recommendation.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Oncologic emergencies and treatment complications
objectives: Recognize time-critical syndromes, stabilize conceptually and escalate; discriminate toxicity from progression/infection.
units.topics: Tumor lysis, febrile neutropenia, cord compression, SVC syndrome, hypercalcemia, immune adverse events, thrombosis, cytopenias.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Oncology: oncologic complications and treatment/care; ABIM Heme overlap.
units.casePractice: Fictional triage scenarios; scoring: identify red flags, differential, escalation/monitoring, avoid unsupported definitive treatment.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Cancer clinical trials, statistics and precision medicine
objectives: Interpret trial design, endpoints, absolute/relative effects, uncertainty and external validity; apply biomarker and genomic evidence responsibly.
units.topics: Phase design, randomization, bias, survival endpoints, NNT caveats, molecular tests, germline/somatic distinction, consent and ethics.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Oncology: clinical research methodology and ethics (6.5%); risk/prognosis; precision oncology.
units.casePractice: Use NCI trial resources. Assignment: one-page critical appraisal; rubric: design, endpoint, effect, harms, population applicability, ethics.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Supportive care, survivorship, communication and equity
objectives: Elicit goals and preferences, communicate prognosis with uncertainty, recognize palliative/supportive needs and access disparities.
units.topics: Pain, symptoms, survivorship, late effects, fertility, psychosocial/spiritual needs, end-of-life, communication, health equity and cost barriers.
units.boardDomains: ABIM Oncology: palliative/survivorship/communication (11%); health equity cross-cutting.
units.casePractice: Use NCI PDQ supportive care. Fictional serious-illness communication role-play scored on listening, plain language, uncertainty, shared decision-making.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

units.title: Integrated board-style synthesis and longitudinal practice
objectives: Integrate diagnostic data with evidence and comorbidities; choose next action, state uncertainty and safety net; reflect on gaps.
units.topics: Cross-specialty cases; test selection, prognosis, treatment decision, complications, trial evidence, prevention and follow-up.
units.boardDomains: Both ABIM certification blueprint task categories and ACGME competencies as a mapping framework, not equivalence.
units.casePractice: Capstone: timed original questions and evidence-backed written rationale. Rubric: clinical reasoning 40%, evidence 25%, safety 20%, communication/equity 15%.
units.assessment: Formative case/data interpretation plus the unit-specific assignment/rubric described in casePractice. Scoring evaluates reasoning, evidence, safety and uncertainty; it is not clinical competency assessment.

assignment: 12-unit longitudinal portfolio: each unit produce one evidence-linked diagnostic/decision map from fictional written scenarios; final case conference compares options, uncertainty, escalation and patient priorities. Use public sources current as of completion; cite evidence and publication dates. Rubric: reasoning and differential 35%, interpretation/evidence 25%, safety/uncertainty 20%, communication/equity 10%, citation quality 10%. No real patient records, patient advice, treatment orders or procedural sign-off.
assessment: Formative quizzes and assignments; 10 original educational multiple-choice items are included. There is no validated cut score, psychometric calibration, clinical assessment, accredited credit or predictor of ABIM passing. Recheck material against current board blueprints and clinical references.

studyHours.basis: Transparent self-study plan: 12 units x 7 hours (84), 12 assignments x 1.5 hours (18), integrated review/question work 18 hours = 120 planned learner hours. This is a planning estimate and is not training credit or observed video runtime.

unitMap.text: Hematology reasoning, CBC/smear and anemia
Hemolysis, hemoglobinopathy and marrow failure
Hemostasis, platelets and thrombosis
Plasma-cell disorders and monoclonal proteins
Leukemias, MDS and myeloproliferative neoplasms
Lymphoma, cellular therapy, transplant and transfusion
Solid-tumor diagnosis, staging and biomarker reasoning
Systemic therapy: cytotoxic, endocrine, targeted and immune
Oncologic emergencies and treatment complications
Cancer clinical trials, statistics and precision medicine
Supportive care, survivorship, communication and equity
Integrated board-style synthesis and longitudinal practice

topicGaps: Verified long-form recordings now add substantial content in mechanism/targeted therapy, immunotherapy, breast, melanoma, lung, prostate, pancreatic and gastric cancer, myeloid genetics, Duffy antigen, cancer-related lymphedema, GI cancer, and supportive/palliative oncology. They do not form a balanced curriculum across every blueprint subtopic.

ABIM Medical Oncology blueprint domains with no directly mapped verified long-form course lecture remain: detailed gynecologic and genitourinary (other than prostate), skin/sarcoma/unknown primary, head/neck/thyroid/CNS malignancies; broad systematic coverage of hematologic malignancy diagnosis and care; trials/ethics; and many complications. Hematology gaps include comprehensive lymphoma, myeloma diagnosis/therapy, transfusion, transplant, CAR T/cellular therapy, and full breadth of coagulation.

Target 36 actual free recording hours remains unmet; the exact remaining difference is hoursGap. Authored scripts and planned clip target minutes do not close the video-hour gap. Further topic-specific recordings should be verified before asserting coverage.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) Hematology Certification Examination
American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) Medical Oncology Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: Two separate ABIM subspecialty certification examinations exist: Hematology and Medical Oncology. Hopkins describes a combined program with independent specialty tracks and single- or dual-certification pathways. This syllabus is not an exam, credential, program listing or eligibility determination.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM eligibility is board-determined and requires prior internal medicine certification, accredited fellowship training, clinical competency and licensure requirements. Dual certification requires board-prescribed combined accredited training and clinical exposure. Self-study, course completion or 36 video hours does not qualify a learner for an exam. Verify current ABIM requirements directly.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine
officialProgrammes.name: Hematology and Medical Oncology Fellowship Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official program page states combined fellowship, with independent Hematology and Medical Oncology tracks, tailored 12-month track curricula, and dual or single certification. Hematology track page describes immersive inpatient/outpatient training and flexible further pathways. Public page does not provide a complete lecture inventory. Individual track and research opportunities are institution-specific. No Harvard-affiliated variant was included in the supplied item packet and this task did not conduct comprehensive directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Exact supplied item: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine Hematology and Medical Oncology Fellowship Program. Its official page distinguishes a combined clinical fellowship from separate Hematology and Medical Oncology tracks; the separate hematology track page describes a focused non-malignant pathway and optional further training. No separate pediatric fellowship, generic directory entry, research-only supplement or non-physician track is merged here. No comprehensive Harvard/Johns Hopkins program-directory audit was completed in this single-item task; packet contains only Hopkins.
sourceCaveats: The official Johns Hopkins page describes a combined fellowship with separate Hematology and Medical Oncology tracks; exact institutional track offerings preserved. Single-board track and dual-board route are not collapsed into separate independent institutions.

The ABIM pages distinguish two separate subspecialty boards/exams. Research pathway is not equivalent to clinical fellowship; research supplements are not included as separate clinical specialties. Pediatric heme-oncology is not included in the adult scope.

ACGME 2026 document reports 36-month combined training requirement effective/revision details; board pathways and program requirements may change. Reconfirm date-sensitive requirements before reliance.
Public institutional pages are not exhaustive formal curricula; rotations, patient volume, case counts, selection/eligibility and unpublished didactics are not inferred.
No patient records or diagnostic images are copied. Public access does not establish reuse permission; link only and check item-specific rights.
Clinical content is educational, date-sensitive and not a substitute for current local protocols, specialty review, clinical care or guidelines. NCI PDQ summaries are explicitly not guidelines.

topicGaps: Verified long-form recordings now add substantial content in mechanism/targeted therapy, immunotherapy, breast, melanoma, lung, prostate, pancreatic and gastric cancer, myeloid genetics, Duffy antigen, cancer-related lymphedema, GI cancer, and supportive/palliative oncology. They do not form a balanced curriculum across every blueprint subtopic.

ABIM Medical Oncology blueprint domains with no directly mapped verified long-form course lecture remain: detailed gynecologic and genitourinary (other than prostate), skin/sarcoma/unknown primary, head/neck/thyroid/CNS malignancies; broad systematic coverage of hematologic malignancy diagnosis and care; trials/ethics; and many complications. Hematology gaps include comprehensive lymphoma, myeloma diagnosis/therapy, transfusion, transplant, CAR T/cellular therapy, and full breadth of coagulation.

Target 36 actual free recording hours remains unmet; the exact remaining difference is hoursGap. Authored scripts and planned clip target minutes do not close the video-hour gap. Further topic-specific recordings should be verified before asserting coverage.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult has microcytic anemia, low ferritin, low transferrin saturation and an inappropriately low reticulocyte response. What mechanism best explains the pattern?

options.text: Iron-restricted erythropoiesis
Acute intravascular hemolysis
Sickle-cell hemolysis
Pure red-cell aplasia from parvovirus

practiceQuestions.rationale: Low iron stores with inadequate marrow response supports iron-restricted production; clinical context and cause of deficiency still require evaluation. Not a diagnosis from one test alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, elevated LDH and neurologic symptoms. Which next reasoning step is most appropriate?

options.text: Consider a thrombotic microangiopathy urgently and distinguish TTP/HUS/DIC while arranging urgent specialist evaluation
Assume immune thrombocytopenia
Order only a platelet antibody and discharge
Diagnose iron deficiency

practiceQuestions.rationale: Thrombocytopenia plus microangiopathic hemolysis and organ findings is an emergency pattern; urgently evaluate TMA differential and do not delay expert care. A vignette cannot establish subtype by itself.

practiceQuestions.stem: A prolonged aPTT corrects on immediate mixing study but becomes prolonged after incubation. This pattern most suggests:

options.text: A time-dependent coagulation-factor inhibitor
A simple factor deficiency only
Platelet dysfunction
Iron deficiency

practiceQuestions.rationale: Time-dependent loss of correction raises an inhibitor such as acquired factor inhibitor; interpret assay details, medications and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional patient with monoclonal protein and anemia, which conclusion is safest before marrow and end-organ criteria are reviewed?

options.text: A monoclonal protein alone does not establish multiple myeloma
All monoclonal proteins indicate symptomatic myeloma
A normal creatinine proves MGUS
SPEP replaces immunofixation and free-light-chain interpretation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Monoclonal proteins span benign precursor states and clinically significant disorders; classification requires integrated laboratory, imaging, marrow and clinical criteria.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which general approach is most appropriate for a suspected acute leukemia?

options.text: Integrate morphology, immunophenotype, cytogenetic/molecular studies and clinical urgency
Classify solely by peripheral WBC count
Start a targeted drug based only on age
Use PET as the sole diagnostic test

practiceQuestions.rationale: Modern classification and risk decisions use integrated pathology and molecular findings; emergencies such as suspected APL require urgent specialist-directed evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with advanced cancer asks about a trial. Which appraisal item is essential before applying published benefit estimates?

options.text: Whether trial population, comparator, endpoint and eligibility resemble this patient and decision
Only the P value
Whether the drug has a biologically plausible target
Whether the study was published in a high-impact journal

practiceQuestions.rationale: Internal validity does not guarantee applicability; assess population, comparator, endpoint, effect size, harms, and the person’s goals.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient is being considered for systemic treatment. Which framework best aligns with the ABIM oncology decision task?

options.text: Integrate disease stage/biology, evidence, intent, comorbidity, risks and informed preferences
Select the newest drug regardless of biomarker
Treat radiographic response as the only goal
Assume a guideline is a substitute for shared decision-making

practiceQuestions.rationale: Board framework emphasizes care decisions; clinical choices require context, current evidence, benefit-harm discussion and preferences.

practiceQuestions.stem: During cancer immunotherapy a fictional patient develops new dyspnea. What is the best educational response?

options.text: Treat as potentially urgent; consider therapy toxicity and competing diagnoses and escalate for clinical assessment
Assume tumor progression only
Reassure because immune toxicities are always mild
Use this online course to prescribe treatment

practiceQuestions.rationale: New dyspnea can reflect treatment toxicity, infection, thromboembolism, progression or other urgent causes. Requires actual clinical evaluation, not remote self-study.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the correct relationship of NCI PDQ health professional summaries to treatment guidelines?

options.text: They are evidence-based summaries and explicitly are not clinical practice guidelines or treatment recommendations
They are legally binding protocols
They guarantee current local standard of care
They replace specialist judgment

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes PDQ summaries as public, expert-reviewed, evidence-based and updated, but says they are not clinical practice guidelines or treatment recommendations.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about this independent course and ABIM certification is accurate?

options.text: It cannot establish ABIM eligibility; certification requires board-defined training/competence and examination requirements
36 video hours equal fellowship training
A passing course quiz grants board eligibility
Single and dual certification use the same single examination

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM policy requires accredited clinical fellowship training and other criteria; Hematology and Medical Oncology have separate certification examinations.

title: Hematology/Oncology Fellowship
prerequisites: Completed foundational medical education equivalent to internal-medicine level pathology, physiology, pharmacology, microbiology, immunology and statistics; this is not a substitute for medical school or residency.
Comfort reading CBC/differential, peripheral smear descriptions, chemistry panels, basic pathology and imaging reports.
Ethics, informed consent, evidence appraisal and privacy awareness.
The course is an advanced independent study syllabus; learners must not use it to make or implement patient-care decisions.
objectives: Integrate clinical presentation, morphology, immunophenotype, molecular results, imaging and disease context into a defensible differential.
Map reasoning to the current distinct ABIM hematology and medical-oncology content blueprints, while recognizing those blueprints are not full clinical curricula.
Use evidence hierarchy, trial design and evolving guidelines to separate historically important findings from current practice.
Recognize time-critical hematologic/oncologic complications and communicate the need for prompt supervised evaluation.
Discuss uncertainty, patient preferences, health equity, survivorship and supportive/palliative care.
Identify where clinical procedures, patient volumes, supervision, program evaluation and procedural competence are not acquired through self-study.

assignment.title: Integrated case conference: monoclonal protein with possible organ injury
assignment.task: Using the fictional scenario in Unit 9, produce a 1,200–1,500-word evidence map: define what is known/unknown; compare MGUS, symptomatic plasma-cell neoplasm and AL amyloid as categories without diagnosing an actual patient; list decision-relevant laboratory, marrow, imaging and organ-attribution evidence; assess source date and uncertainty; and explain why PYP uptake alone does not type amyloid. Do not provide a drug regimen or patient-specific plan.

rubric.standard: Separates clonal protein, disease category and organ injury; identifies missing data and attribution uncertainty.
Cites current ASH and NCI material; states date/version and distinguishes guideline, blueprint and training standard.
Does not overcall myeloma, label PYP pathognomonic for ATTR, or give real-patient orders.
Explains uncertainty, patient preferences, accessible communication and referral/oversight boundaries.
Concise, reproducible evidence map with claims linked to sources.

assignment.passThreshold: 80/100 for this course assignment only; not a board predictor or competence determination.

assessment.format: Unit retrieval checks, original case-based single-best-answer items, a written evidence map and reflective error log.
assessment.courseCriterion: Suggested completion standard: at least 80% on course-authored quizzes after feedback and submission of assignment. This is formative self-study only.
assessment.limitations: Questions are original, not official ABIM content, not validated, and cannot predict or guarantee passing. No clinical procedural assessment, patient-care observation or independent practice evaluation is provided.

studyHours.breakdown: 12 units x 8 hours guided reading/case reasoning (96 hours), 12 hours retrieval practice/question rationales, 8 hours assignment and revision, 4 hours course-level blueprint/error-log synthesis. This is a planning estimate for independent study, not observed training or video runtime. Actual study time varies.

unitMap.text: Clinical reasoning, cancer biology, and evidence navigation
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: internal-medicine level physiology, pathology, pharmacology, statistics.
Clinical context, incidence and screening vs diagnostic workup; clonal hematopoiesis; tumor biology; staging/prognostic systems; pathology/molecular testing overview; evidence hierarchy.

unitMap.text: Supportive oncology, emergencies, and treatment toxicity
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: acute care and pharmacology.

Oncologic emergencies; febrile neutropenia principles; nausea, mucositis, cytopenias, renal/hepatic toxicity; immune toxicities; symptom control, nutrition, infection prevention, fertility and survivorship.

unitMap.text: Diagnostic foundations, pathology, cytogenetics and precision oncology
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: pathology, genetics, test characteristics.
Biopsy adequacy; immunohistochemistry; flow; karyotype/FISH/NGS; tumor-agnostic biomarkers; germline vs somatic testing; liquid biopsy; clonal hematopoiesis; tissue stewardship.

unitMap.text: Systemic therapy mechanisms, clinical trials, and immunotherapy
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: cell biology, pharmacology, epidemiology.
Phase I–III designs; randomization; intention-to-treat; surrogates; targeted therapy; immune checkpoints; CAR T and bispecific concepts; toxicity reporting; ethics.

unitMap.text: Thoracic cancer: lung, mesothelioma, and thymic tumors
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: pathology, imaging literacy.
NSCLC, SCLC, mesothelioma, thymic malignancies; molecular testing; metastatic presentations; brain metastasis and thoracic toxicities.

unitMap.text: Gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary cancers
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: anatomy, pathology, molecular basics.
Colorectal, gastric, esophageal, pancreas, biliary, hepatocellular, small bowel, appendiceal, anal and GI neuroendocrine disease; hereditary cancer; treatment toxicities.

unitMap.text: Breast, genitourinary, gynecologic, skin, CNS, head/neck, sarcoma
coveredTopics: Prerequisite: pathology, reproductive and GU anatomy.

topicGaps: Verified observed accessible recordings total 16.958 hours; 19.042 hours remain below the 36-hour target. Original scripts and minute targets are not rendered video and do not reduce this gap.

No sufficiently comprehensive, current, openly accessible lecture sequence was verified for lymphoma subtypes, CLL/SLL, multiple myeloma/current AL pathways, ALL, MDS/MPN breadth, transfusion practice beyond the single focused talk, HCT/GVHD, CAR-T toxicities, and most GI/GU/gynecologic/CNS/head-and-neck/sarcoma topics.

Included 2014–2015-era UofL materials and 2018-era/other dated items provide historical concepts only. Disease-specific therapy, screening, thresholds and eligibility require current primary guidelines and expert review.

The Yale 2025 grand-rounds additions supply selected disease-topic depth, not a complete fellowship didactic programme or full board blueprint coverage. Public institutional fellowship pages remain high-level; no private teaching material was obtained.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) Hematology Certification Examination
American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) Medical Oncology Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: Two distinct ABIM subspecialty certifications and separate certification exams exist: Hematology and Medical Oncology. Hopkins presents one combined fellowship with distinct single-board tracks and an optional dual-certification pathway. The generic combined directory category is not a third board exam.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent study curriculum provides no ABIM eligibility. ABIM eligibility depends on the applicable prior certification, required accredited graduate medical education, competency attestations, licensure and examination rules in force at application. A course, attendance record or video total cannot substitute for accredited training, clinical competence or board approval. Hopkins public pages describe track options but do not confer eligibility. Confirm current rules directly with ABIM and the accredited program.

medical.programmeSourceScope: For MED-116 the supplied packet identifies Johns Hopkins only. Exact institutional variants preserved here: combined fellowship program; its Medical Oncology Track; its Hematology Track. They are not three unrelated physician specialties and are not triple-counted. Hematology/Medical Oncology is a physician clinical fellowship; it is not a research-only position, non-physician program, pediatric fellowship, pathology hematopathology fellowship, or generic directory category. The Hematology Track page notes added complementary training options (including med-peds pediatric heme-onc) but those are not included as separate pediatric board tracks here. Input packet notes Hopkins directory category “ACGME Accredited or Equivalent”; this research did not independently resolve a current institution-specific ACGME accreditation record. Current ACGME program requirements were checked as standards, not as proof of Hopkins accreditation.
sourceCaveats: Institutional pages expose only high-level track descriptions, not the full official curriculum, all rotations, lecture sets, workload or case volume. ACGME standards are not evidence of Hopkins-specific current accreditation. The packet supplied an ACGME-or-equivalent directory label; independent status verification remains open.

ABIM hematology and medical-oncology exams are distinct. ABIM states certification eligibility requires relevant prior certification, accredited training, competence, unrestricted licensure and passing exam; this independent course confers none of these. Exam requirements may change; confirm directly with ABIM.

The January 2026 Medical Oncology blueprint states content priorities apply beginning Fall 2026. Hematology and Medical Oncology content distributions differ and have been mapped separately at unit level.

NCI PDQ page for plasma-cell neoplasms shows latest update 2025-04-25, so current guideline checking is essential. ASH Amyloidosis page identifies 2026 diagnostic guidelines and says its treatment panel will follow.

No protected institutional or ABIM materials, paid content or private patient data were accessed. YouTube and image repositories are linked, not copied or embedded; public viewing does not grant redistribution rights.

Three dated videos are counted only after their public durations were visible in source metadata; historical content is not endorsed as current guidance. Unknown-duration candidates and unavailable clips are not counted.
The course does not include any separate research-only or non-physician training track and no pediatric track is claimed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has microcytosis, low ferritin and low transferrin saturation. Which process most directly explains this pattern?

options.text: Iron depletion limiting hemoglobin synthesis
Increased globin-chain synthesis
Acute hemolysis with reticulocytosis
Isolated factor VIII deficiency

practiceQuestions.rationale: Low ferritin with microcytosis supports depleted iron stores; determine the cause of deficiency rather than treating an isolated laboratory pattern. This is an educational vignette, not a complete clinical work-up.

practiceQuestions.stem: A small monoclonal protein is found in an older adult with no attributable end-organ injury. What is the best conceptual next step?

options.text: Assume symptomatic myeloma and treat
Classify the clone using clinical, laboratory, marrow and imaging context before assigning a plasma-cell category
Ignore all monoclonal proteins below a fixed concentration
Diagnose AL amyloidosis from M-protein alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: A monoclonal protein alone does not establish myeloma or AL amyloidosis. NCI PDQ describes integrated assessment including monoclonal protein, marrow, imaging and organ injury.

practiceQuestions.stem: A cancer patient develops unilateral leg swelling. Which statement best reflects a sound diagnostic-reasoning approach?

options.text: A cancer history proves DVT
Use clinical assessment and appropriate objective testing; consider alternatives and bleeding risk
A D-dimer alone confirms thrombosis in all cancer patients
Start prophylaxis as a substitute for diagnostic evaluation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Cancer increases VTE risk but does not establish the diagnosis. Use current diagnostic pathways and patient context; ASH guidance is linked for review.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient on checkpoint inhibition presents with dyspnea and new pulmonary opacities. What is the best board-style first reasoning move?

options.text: Assume cancer progression only
Consider urgent treatment-related immune toxicity alongside infection, progression and other causes; assess severity
Continue therapy without evaluation
Call this a confirmed immune pneumonitis based on exposure alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Exposure is a clue, not a diagnosis; a safe differential includes toxicity, infection and progression. Clinical assessment is required; this course provides no orders.

practiceQuestions.stem: A tumor board reviews a trial reporting improved median progression-free survival but no mature overall-survival data. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.text: The surrogate endpoint proves cure
Assess absolute effect, uncertainty, harms, follow-up and whether the endpoint is validated for the setting
Ignore randomization
Convert the median difference directly into an individual survival guarantee

practiceQuestions.rationale: Board-style evidence reasoning distinguishes endpoints, absolute effect and uncertainty. ABIM oncology blueprint explicitly tests clinical research methodology and ethics.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, neurologic symptoms and renal injury. What response best fits exam reasoning?

options.text: Treat as routine iron deficiency
Recognize a potentially time-critical thrombotic microangiopathy differential and escalate urgent specialist evaluation
Assume immune thrombocytopenia from platelet count alone
Wait for a routine outpatient repeat CBC

practiceQuestions.rationale: The pattern raises urgent TMA/TTP/HUS and other causes; the question tests recognition/escalation, not a treatment protocol. Hematology blueprint includes these diagnoses.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has an M-protein and increased cardiac tracer uptake on scintigraphy. Which statement is safest?

options.text: Tracer uptake alone proves transthyretin amyloidosis
A monoclonal protein excludes any amyloid diagnosis
Do not use tracer uptake alone as typing; evaluate for AL/monoclonal disease and follow an appropriate validated typing pathway
A normal CBC proves there is no plasma-cell disorder

practiceQuestions.rationale: PYP uptake is not pathognomonic for ATTR. AL must be considered when a monoclonal protein is present; ASH 2026 provides current diagnostic guidance. No imaging or diagnostic result is supplied here.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with fever during myelosuppressive therapy is hypotensive. What is the priority concept?

options.text: Routine follow-up after nadir
Treat as an emergency requiring rapid assessment for sepsis/febrile neutropenia and escalation
Wait for confirmatory marrow results
Assume a drug allergy

practiceQuestions.rationale: Fever with hemodynamic instability in an oncology patient is an emergency. Exact empiric treatment depends on clinician assessment/local protocols and is outside this study vignette.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which choice best describes a transfusion-reaction reasoning step?

options.text: Continue the transfusion while symptoms are investigated
Stop and promptly evaluate a suspected reaction under local protocol; distinguish categories with clinical/lab data
Assume all post-transfusion fever is hemolysis
Use a photomicrograph as the sole diagnostic basis

practiceQuestions.rationale: Suspected transfusion reaction requires prompt safety response and structured assessment; specific procedures require supervised institutional training.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with advanced cancer expresses a goal of maximizing time at home and avoiding burdensome treatment. What is the best communication approach?

options.text: Avoid discussing prognosis
Explore values, explain options and uncertainty, and align recommendations with the patient’s stated goals
Promise a survival duration
Assume palliative care means stopping all cancer-directed therapy

practiceQuestions.rationale: Patient-centered decision-making involves goals and uncertainty; palliative care can coexist with cancer-directed treatment. Medical Oncology blueprint assigns substantial weight to palliative care, survivorship and communication.

topicGaps: The publicly observed, unique ready-recording ledger totals 17.9353 hours; the 36-hour floor still has a residual of 18.0647 hours. Authored scripts and target minutes are not rendered media and contribute zero.

Current accessible recordings are unevenly distributed: disease-specific material is concentrated in thoracic cancer, pancreatic tumor biology, ovarian hereditary risk, germ-cell biology, bladder mechanisms, glioblastoma and head/neck care-access research. Several are mechanistic or research talks, not clinical decision lessons.

No suitable verified current full-length recordings were located for comprehensive breast treatment, prostate and renal-cell clinical pathways, hematologic disease-group breadth, cervical/endometrial/uterine sarcoma, colorectal/hepatobiliary/upper-GI/NET disease management, melanoma, sarcoma, unknown primary, thyroid/salivary/nasopharyngeal cancers, or broad evidence-appraisal/trial-ethics instruction.

Treatment complications are only sampled (tumor lysis and cardio-oncology); the recording set does not supply comprehensive current toxicity triage, dose/contraindication teaching, or clinical protocols.

Palliative and survivorship coverage is inadequate: one emerging psychedelic/regulatory research talk is not a general symptom/pain-management curriculum. Communication, end-of-life, fertility, late effects, cost/access and equity need additional current source-led episodes and qualified review.

Older 2014 breast metastasis biology and any experimental/mechanistic recording require explicit separation from dated efficacy/indication claims. The unknown-duration Sylvester 2017 videos remain uncounted.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Medical Oncology Certification Examination
ABIM Hematology Certification Examination — separate examination; relevant only for dual certification
American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Pediatric Hematology-Oncology Certification Examination; separate pediatric track, excluded from this adult curriculum
medical.boardStatus: ABIM has a distinct Medical Oncology subspecialty certification examination. Adult Hematology/Oncology training may support separate hematology and medical oncology certification only when all current board requirements are met. The public Dana-Farber/MGB page also describes a distinct Classical Hematology track and links a separate pediatric programme; neither should be conflated with this adult medical-oncology self-study course.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Course participation does not establish eligibility. ABIM eligibility includes prior ABIM internal medicine certification, requisite accredited fellowship training, clinical competence/procedural skills, unrestricted license, and passing the exam. Dual Hematology/Medical Oncology certification has separate combined-training requirements. The pediatric programme has a separate ABP path. Verify current requirements directly with the board.
